query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) knockdown has been shown to suppress cyclin D1 expression and inhibit cell proliferation, while promoting apoptosis [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. MIF knockdown in HCC cells downregulated the expression of growth-related proteins such as cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, while upregulating pro-apoptotic proteins like Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. However, another study focused on TNF-alpha-induced protein 8-like 2 (TIPE2) rather than MIF, and found that TIPE2 suppresses HCC metastasis by inhibiting Rac1 [pmc_PMC4176125||ABSTRACT||000]. The knockdown of TIPE2 was associated with increased tumor cell growth, migration, and invasion in vitro, and enhanced growth and metastasis of HCC in vivo [pmc_PMC4176125||ABSTRACT||000]. While these findings do not directly address MIF, they highlight the importance of regulatory proteins in HCC progression.

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Coronary artery calcifications (CAC) are associated with an increased risk of complications and adverse outcomes. Left main coronary artery calcification is independently associated with the development of any complication, with an odds ratio of 3.9 (95% CI 1.7–8.9) [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. An increasing number of calcified coronary arteries shows a trend toward an association with complications (p = 0.07) and is significantly associated with an adverse discharge condition (p = 0.02) [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. Additionally, CAC scores predict mortality in symptomatic patients, with a median score of 0 in women and 42 in men, and a median follow-up of 4.4 years showed that 2.3% of patients died [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. Heavily calcified coronary lesions can be effectively treated using orbital atherectomy, which results in high device success (66%) and procedural success (94%) [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. However, while CAC and carotid artery intima-media thickness (cIMT) and plaque are associated with the future risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) independent of conventional risk factors [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000], no clinical trial has assessed whether screening with CAC or cIMT/plaque leads to improved clinical outcomes and healthcare costs [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
final_answer: The learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction showed significant improvements over time, as evidenced by a reduction in both the length of hospital stay and the total surgery time. For single DIEP flaps, the hospital stay decreased from 7.1 ± 1.8 days in the early group to 6.3 ± 1.5 days in the late group (p = 0.019), and for double DIEP flaps, it decreased from 8.5 ± 3.8 days to 6.6 ± 1.4 days (p = 0.043) [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, the total surgery time for the single surgeon decreased significantly over time, further indicating a positive trend in the learning curve [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. These improvements suggest that the surgeon's experience and proficiency increased, leading to better patient outcomes and more efficient surgical procedures.

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models in mice are essential for understanding the molecular mechanisms of cardiac regeneration, as these models demonstrate that the neonatal heart retains full regenerative capacity after injury [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. This regenerative capacity is not observed in adult hearts, but the insights gained from neonatal models can help identify factors that stimulate endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation in adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. By studying these mechanisms, researchers can develop novel therapeutic strategies for cardiac regeneration in adults, potentially translating findings from neonatal models to adult cardiac repair.

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Mask mandates can significantly reduce the growth rate of COVID-19 cases, particularly when combined with proper ventilation and other protective measures. A study found that the combination of face masks and upward ventilation can reduce indoor infectious concentration by nearly 99.95% compared to no precautions [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study estimated that a national mask mandate, if enacted on May 15, 2020, would have reduced total infections in the US by 23.7 to 30.4 percent by November 15, 2020 [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, longer durations of mask mandates (≥2 months) were associated with lower incidence of COVID-19, especially in counties with higher social vulnerability, where the differences in marginal mean monthly incidence ranged from –4 to –401 cases per 100,000 population [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. Proper training in the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is also crucial, particularly for healthcare workers, to maximize the effectiveness of masks [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. However, mask mandates can be ineffective if not combined with proper ventilation, and inappropriate placement of masks with poor ventilation can be counterproductive [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?

Additionally, nano-enhanced biolubricants (NEBL) improve tool wear and surface integrity in minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) machining, further reducing the risk of workpiece burn [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. These properties are particularly beneficial when machining materials like titanium alloys and nickel-based alloys, where preventing wheel wear and surface burn is crucial [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Microplastics (MPs) in fishmeal pose a significant threat to global public health by accumulating in the edible portions of cultured fish, potentially causing severe physiological disorders in fish consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. The introduction of MPs into aquaculture systems via fishmeal can alter the physiological and behavioral attributes of cultured fish, impacting the entire pond ecosystem and leading to potential health risks for human consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, microplastics can serve as a localized source of environmental contamination and a pathway for harmful contaminants in the food chain, posing serious consequences for human health [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. The presence of hazardous chemicals, such as persistent organic pollutants, on the surface of MPs can lead to their transfer through fishmeal, threatening global public health [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. In regions like Africa, microplastics from mismanaged plastic waste pose severe environmental and public health threats, including the development of metal toxicity in aquatic organisms and disruptions to the food chain [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000]. In Bangladesh, commercial fish feeds are 100% contaminated with microplastics, with the mean abundance ranging from 500 to 2200 MPs/kg, and the most common shape being fibers [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. The consumption of seafood contaminated with microplastics can lead to public health challenges for humans, contributing to the global public health threat [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The translational regulation of NEDD4 is intricately linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, particularly in cancer cells that depend on this pathway. In pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells, NEDD4 is translationally upregulated and this upregulation is linked to the PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000]. Similarly, in gastric cancer (GC) cells, NEDD4 expression is higher in IGF1-high tissues compared to IGF1-low tissues and normal tissues, and this co-expression predicts a worse prognosis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. NEDD4 specifically promotes the proliferation of GC cells that are dependent on IGF1/IGF1R signaling by antagonizing the protein phosphatase activity of PTEN to IRS1, thereby regulating Akt activation and tumor growth [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. In PDAC cells, depletion of NEDD4 decreases proliferation and migration, and it affects the PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, suggesting that NEDD4 plays a critical role in activating this pathway by negatively regulating PTEN levels [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. These findings highlight the importance of NEDD4 in the context of cells that depend on the IGF1 signaling pathway for their growth and survival.

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: Textile waste management can effectively utilize waste conversion and the adsorption properties of textile materials to create sustainable solutions. Biotechnological processes, such as using micro-organisms and enzymes, can convert textile waste into valuable products and clean energy [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001]. Additionally, the adsorption properties of textile materials can be harnessed to remove pollutants like dyes and metals from wastewater, making it a cost-effective and feasible process [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. These adsorption properties are crucial for tertiary treatment, complementing primary and secondary treatments that alone may not meet discharge or reuse standards [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. Chemical valorization methods, such as acid hydrolysis and enzymatic recycling, can achieve significant glucose recovery and reduce energy consumption, enhancing the economic viability of waste conversion [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000]. Laboratory-scale processes, like mechanical agitation and cellulase-catalyzed hydrolysis, can disintegrate cotton fabrics, though reactive dyes can inhibit this process [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000]. Companies like Sateri have developed methods to convert post-consumer textile waste into recycled fibers, promoting a sustainable cycle in the fashion industry [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
final_answer: Sustainability reporting is increasingly recognized as a crucial tool for aligning corporate strategies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and enhancing long-term interests, although there are significant challenges in its implementation and effectiveness. While some studies, such as one focusing on the tourism sector, highlight a gap where companies often fail to explain how significant sustainability initiatives impact their business contribution to SDGs [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000], others demonstrate a positive and significant relationship between sustainability reporting, SDG implementation, and financial performance, particularly in the context of sustainable supply chains [https://openalex.org/W4394886303||ABSTRACT||001]. A sustainability assessment framework with 91 performance indicators can enhance transparency and accountability in global supply chains, aligning with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and the SDGs [https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the connection between sustainability reporting and specific SDGs is often weak, with reports lacking life cycle thinking and insufficient sustainability discussions for workers, consumers, and value chain actors [https://openalex.org/W4281493513||ABSTRACT||001]. Despite these gaps, the use of a materiality matrix as a reporting tool can enhance the content of sustainability reports by aligning with stakeholders' perspectives, which is crucial for the supply chain framework [https://openalex.org/W4200252599||ABSTRACT||001]. The integrated reporting system, while valuable, has fundamental flaws that make it challenging to compare between companies, underscoring the need for common metrics to evaluate the implementation of sustainability strategies [https://openalex.org/W4362609606||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
final_answer: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, five multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods—Weighted Sum Model (WSM), Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS), Preference Ranking Organisation METHod for Enrichment of Evaluations (PROMETHEE), ELimination Et Choix Traduisant la REalité (ELECTRE), and Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA)—were compared [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The sensitivity analysis indicated that all methods are suitable for sustainability assessments, but they exhibit differences in their calculation processes and the interpretation of results [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Specifically, the sensitivity analysis involved varying criteria weights individually and by fixed values, as well as comparing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weighting method to an equal weight scenario [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, the fuzzy complex proportional assessment (COPRAS) method was found to be robust, as altering the criteria weights did not significantly affect the ranking of service providers [https://openalex.org/W4281388694||ABSTRACT||001]. These findings suggest that while multiple MCDA methods can be effectively used for sustainability assessments, the choice of method should consider the specific context and criteria of the district heating system being evaluated.

However, the research also notes a gap between the current and intended state of environmental sustainability in manufacturing, indicating that more efforts are needed to align production paradigms with sustainability goals [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||000]. Collaboration among researchers, policymakers, and industry practitioners is essential to develop strategies that leverage Industry 4.0 innovations for environmental sustainability [https://openalex.org/W4392974914||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How are the SDOs linked to policy coherance for sustainable development in the EU context?
final_answer: The linkage between sustainable development organizations (SDOs) and policy coherence for sustainable development (PCSD) in the EU context is multifaceted and involves various strategies and frameworks. Environmental goals within the SDGs, particularly in the EU, are identified as the most complex and least coherent, highlighting the need for improved data availability and monitoring to enhance policy coherence [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. The integration of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and the Planetary Boundaries (PBs) framework can strengthen EU policies by providing a holistic approach to production and consumption and aligning with the physical limits of the planet [https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, a 3D-mapping approach has been proposed to align Country-specific recommendations (CSRs), the SDGs, and the European Green Deal (EGD), which can support EU policymakers in enhancing national recovery plans [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||000]. However, while the EU has integrated the SDGs into its strategic priorities, there are still areas for improvement, particularly in addressing major and significant challenges [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||001]. The circular economy (CE) is also seen as a key mechanism for achieving the SDGs, with research focusing on the homogeneity of the 2030 Agenda objectives and the correlations between CE implementation and the SDGs [https://openalex.org/W3209532954||ABSTRACT||000]. In the Netherlands, institutional arrangements for PCSD aim to resolve policy incoherence but often present an apolitical façade that limits transformative potential [https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000]. Research fields such as governance, circular economy, and decision-making are crucial for enhancing PCSD, and a system perspective is recommended to address identified gaps and boost coherence across different governance levels [https://openalex.org/W4366975340||ABSTRACT||001]. Finally, the political drivers of PCSD, including ideas, institutions, and interests, are critical in understanding how policy coherence is influenced and applied [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The 87 life cycle assessment (LCA) studies were selected using a combination of keyword searches and specific screening criteria. The studies were identified from the Scopus database using the keywords 'Sustainability assessment' OR 'Life cycle assessment' AND 'Internal combustion engine*' OR 'ICE*,' and were published between 2017 and 2023 [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. The PRISMA protocol was used to screen and classify these studies, involving an evaluation matrix to synthesize research evidence [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. The classification was based on six aspects: sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies (including alternative fuels), types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. Additionally, the studies were classified according to the type of LCA approach used (e.g., stand-alone LCA, LCC combined with other analyses) and specific indicators such as global warming potential, eutrophication, human toxicity, and ecotoxicity [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000], [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||001]. Despite these criteria, gaps were identified in the LCA assessments, including limited consideration of environmental pollution, human health, socio-economic aspects, and the fuel production process [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: Research on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has shown that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) plays a significant role in tumor progression. MIF knockdown using siRNA has been found to suppress cyclin D1 expression and inhibit HCC cell proliferation both in vitro and in an in vivo xenograft model [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. This knockdown also promoted apoptosis in HCC cells, as evidenced by the upregulation of Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, and the downregulation of cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. While another study focused on TIPE2, which is involved in suppressing HCC metastasis, it did not directly address MIF [pmc_PMC4176125||ABSTRACT||000], indicating a need for further research to explore the interplay between MIF and other regulatory proteins in HCC.

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Coronary artery calcifications (CAC) are strongly associated with an increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and complications, independent of conventional risk factors [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. CAC scores (CACS) have been shown to improve risk prediction when added to global risk models like the Framingham risk score [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, CACS are predictive of all-cause mortality in symptomatic patients, with higher median scores observed in men compared to women [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. Specifically, left main coronary artery calcification is independently associated with a higher risk of developing complications, with an odds ratio of 3.9 (95% CI 1.7–8.9) [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. An increasing number of calcified coronary arteries also showed a trend toward an association with complications and was significantly linked to adverse discharge conditions [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. However, heavily calcified lesions can be effectively treated with orbital atherectomy, demonstrating high procedural success and safety [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models are essential for understanding the mechanisms of cardiac regeneration, which can subsequently inform the development of therapeutic strategies for adult hearts. These models leverage the unique regenerative capacity of the neonatal heart, which is capable of inducing endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Microplastics (MPs) in fishmeal pose a significant threat to global public health, primarily through their role as a pathway for environmental contamination and the introduction of harmful substances into the food chain [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. The presence of MPs in fishmeal can lead to metal toxicity and disruptions in the food chain, ultimately affecting human health through the consumption of contaminated fish and other seafood [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000]. In aquaculture systems, MPs can accumulate in fishmeal, causing severe physiological disorders in both fish and human consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, the accumulation of MPs in fishmeal can alter the physiological and behavioral attributes of cultured fish, further impacting the pond ecosystem and contributing to the accumulation of MPs in the edible portions of fish [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001]. In Bangladesh, all sampled commercial fish feeds were contaminated with microplastics, with a mean abundance ranging from 500 to 2200 MPs/kg, highlighting the widespread nature of this issue [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. These findings underscore the urgent need for better management of plastic waste and regulation of microplastic contamination in fishmeal to mitigate the potential health risks.

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The translational regulation of NEDD4 is intricately linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, particularly in cells that depend on this pathway. In gastric cancer (GC) cells, NEDD4 promotes proliferation by antagonizing the protein phosphatase activity of PTEN to IRS1, a key component of the IGF1 signaling pathway [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000]. This effect is specific to IGF1R-dependent GC cells and not observed in IGF1R-independent cells [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Clinically, NEDD4 expression is higher in IGF1-high GC tissues compared to IGF1-low and normal tissues, and co-high expression of NEDD4 and IGF1 is associated with a worse prognosis in GC patients [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Additionally, in pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells, NEDD4 is translationally upregulated and plays a critical role in activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway by negatively regulating PTEN levels, which is essential for the proliferation and metastasis of PDAC cells [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000], [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. These findings highlight the importance of NEDD4 in the context of IGF1-dependent cells and its role in promoting cancer progression through the modulation of key signaling pathways.

query: How are the SDOs linked to policy coherance for sustainable development in the EU context?
final_answer: The Sustainable Development Objectives (SDOs) in the EU context are linked to policy coherence for sustainable development through various mechanisms, but challenges remain. The environmental goals within the SDGs are particularly complex and less coherent, necessitating improvements in data availability and monitoring to enhance policy coherence [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. The EU-27 countries' sustainable development index (SDG9) is used to evaluate the implementation of Goal 9, underscoring the importance of coherent policies for infrastructure, industrialization, and innovation [https://openalex.org/W4362550191||ABSTRACT||000]. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is identified as a tool that can support EU policies and the SDGs, enhancing policy design and monitoring [https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. A 3D-mapping approach has been proposed to align Country-specific recommendations (CSRs), the SDGs, and the European Green Deal (EGD) for coherent policy-making, although gaps remain in the CSRs [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||001]. The circular economy (CE) is seen as a potential driver for achieving the SDGs, with research exploring the correlations between CE implementation and the 2030 Agenda [https://openalex.org/W3209532954||ABSTRACT||000]. An analytical framework focusing on the political drivers of policy coherence, such as ideas, institutions, and interests, is also crucial for understanding how coherence is applied [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000]. In the Netherlands, and by extension in the EU, PCSD is embedded in the SDGs, but institutional arrangements often focus on 'neutral' setups, which can limit transformative potential [https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000]. Transdisciplinary research is needed to improve intra-cluster connections and enhance policy coherence in areas like governance, circular economy, and decision-making [https://openalex.org/W4366975340||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The 87 life cycle assessment studies were selected and categorized using a combination of screening criteria and classification rules. The screening criteria included the identification of the most appropriate CE indicators based on criteria levels, performance, loops, unit, dimension, and transversality [https://openalex.org/W4388662253||ABSTRACT||000], as well as the use of the PRISMA protocol, which involved setting up an evaluation matrix to gather and synthesize research evidence [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. Additionally, studies were selected from the Scopus database using specific keywords and then screened based on six aspects: sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies, types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. The classification rules involved the selection of material circularity, product circularity, and longevity indicators as the most suitable for the C-LCSA framework [https://openalex.org/W4388662253||ABSTRACT||001]. Studies were also classified according to the type of life cycle approach used, such as stand-alone LCA, LCC, and S-LCA [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||001]. The screening process identified studies published between 2017 and 2023, and highlighted gaps such as limited focus on environmental pollution, human health, socio-economic aspects, fuel production, maintenance, small and developing countries, emerging ICE technologies, and large mobile sources [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided papers, coronary artery calcification is generally associated with worse outcomes, but the specific complications vary by setting. In a symptomatic outpatient cardiology cohort, higher coronary artery calcium score (CACS) predicted all-cause mortality over a median 4.4 years, and absolute CACS was at least as informative as sex- and race/ethnicity-specific percentiles for death prediction [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. A review also summarizes prior studies showing that CAC is associated with future atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk independent of conventional risk factors and improves risk prediction when added to a global model such as the Framingham risk score [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In level-1 trauma patients, left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with any in-hospital complication, and an increasing number of calcified coronary arteries showed a trend toward complications and was significantly associated with adverse discharge condition [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. The trauma study therefore supports an acute-care complication signal for visible coronary calcification on routine CT, whereas the outpatient cardiology study highlights long-term mortality risk [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the review notes that similar CAC levels can correspond to different absolute ASCVD risks across regions and ethnic groups, suggesting that the complication risk is not uniform across populations [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers in the set do not provide direct evidence on calcification-related complications, and one severe-calcification intervention study reported high procedural success and no primary safety events over 30 days without giving specific complication rates beyond that [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: In the provided evidence, the only paper directly addressing KAI1 and VEGF in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) reports that serum KAI1 is downregulated and VEGF is upregulated in HCC patients, and that each marker has diagnostic value on its own, with an AUC of 0.907 for KAI1 and 0.779 for VEGF [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study found that combining KAI1 and VEGF improved diagnostic performance over KAI1 alone, increasing sensitivity from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy from 83.06% to 84.68%, while yielding a negative predictive value of 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors conclude that the combined assay may greatly improve HCC diagnosis and could serve as a reliable diagnostic marker panel [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. No other supplied summaries provide additional evidence about KAI1, VEGF, or combined detection for HCC, so the synthesis relies entirely on this single study [pmc_PMC8318739||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests that the combined detection is intended to improve diagnostic performance beyond either marker alone, but the magnitude of improvement is modest and specifically documented only relative to KAI1 alone in the supplied summary [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].

The same abstract also reports that, for the single surgeon, total surgery time decreased significantly across the study period, indicating greater operative efficiency with experience [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. Beyond these changes, the abstract states that there were no other statistically significant differences between the start and end of the study period at the institutional level [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. The other provided papers do not add DIEP-specific learning-curve information: one is about machine learning in breast surgery generally, another about immediate reconstruction uptake in older women, and another about revision/secondary reconstruction patterns rather than DIEP learning over time [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364779||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence supports a modest but clear improvement over time in DIEP reconstruction efficiency, mainly reflected by shorter length of stay and reduced operative time, while other outcomes are not reported as changing [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models appear useful for understanding adult heart cardiac regeneration because newborn mice retain a brief period of full regenerative capacity after cardiac injury, making them a tractable in vivo system for studying the molecular mechanisms of regeneration [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. These models are described as important for identifying factors that could stimulate regeneration in adult hearts, particularly by promoting endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which is a major therapeutic goal for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. More broadly, mammalian neonatal models are presented as translational platforms for testing drugs and treatments aimed at cardiac regeneration, and their findings may guide regenerative medicine alongside large animal and human studies [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study suggests that neonatal injury responses can illuminate how the heart’s transcriptional program differs under distinct stress conditions, with chronic ISO/PE treatment in neonates inducing changes in extracellular matrix, fiber organization, metabolism, muscle adaptation, and electrophysiology [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. That neonatal stress signature was reported to more closely resemble early transcriptional changes seen in pressure overload-induced experimental heart failure and human hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, supporting the idea that neonatal models can connect early injury responses to adult disease-remodeling patterns [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the summaries support a view that neonatal injury models help adult-heart research by revealing regenerative biology, candidate pro-regenerative factors, and stress-response programs that may overlap with adult pathology [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence provided is limited to summary-level statements, and one neonatal study specifically emphasizes similarity to adult heart disease remodeling rather than directly demonstrating adult regeneration [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. Several other papers provided in the set do not address neonatal injury models or adult cardiac regeneration at all, so they add no direct evidence to the question [pmc_PMC9762362||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9889319||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806425||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10230358||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10230358||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10143004||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The ClinicalTrials.gov record summarized in the evidence describes the DECISION study as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial in patients with locally advanced/metastatic radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), designed to test whether sorafenib improves progression-free survival (PFS) [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Treatment continued until radiographically documented disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days (2 cycles), while safety assessments were done every 28 days (1 cycle) for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The primary endpoint was PFS, and secondary endpoints included overall survival, time to disease progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetic analysis [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The trial registration identifier reported for this DECISION phase III study is NCT00984282 [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Other supplied summaries mention different DECISION-related trial registration numbers and outcome sets, but they do not provide matching phase III design details or treatment schedules, so they cannot be used to further define this specific ClinicalTrials.gov record [pmc_PMC9806070||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC10387733||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806046||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5387979||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC9806091||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraq study from Mosul/Nineveh governorates, broiler chicks from imported Cobb 500 and Ross 308 flocks were compared for maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination using 707 blood samples from 28 Ross 308 flocks and 17 Cobb 500 flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Both strains showed high and fairly uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 performed better overall [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Specifically, Cobb 500 had 100% positivity versus 97.78% in Ross 308, a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), and a lower mean CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%) [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The study also reported a higher vaccination index for Cobb 500 than Ross 308 (966.59 vs 821.60), supporting the conclusion that Cobb 500 chicks had higher protective titers [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. No other provided paper offered relevant evidence on this Newcastle disease comparison in Iraqi broiler chicks, so the strain-specific conclusion rests entirely on this study [pmc_PMC8703754||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10059746||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC4172590||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4367043336||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Mask mandates appear to help reduce COVID-19 cases by lowering transmission when they are adopted and followed consistently, and several studies in the summaries support this effect at different levels of evidence [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000]. In US state-level data, the study found that mask mandates could offset about one third of the increase in case growth associated with a rise in mobility, and a hypothetical national mandate on May 15, 2020 was estimated to reduce total infections by 23.7% to 30.4% by November 15, 2020 [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study found that mask mandates in place for at least two months were associated with lower monthly incidence than having no prevention measure or having one in place for less than a month, with larger reductions seen in high-social-vulnerability counties [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. The healthcare-worker reviews also found that face masks significantly protected against infection, with especially strong support for N95 masks, while surgical masks were reported to protect better than cloth masks [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. One modeling paper adds that masks work best when combined with upward ventilation, whereas masks used inappropriately with ventilation could be counterproductive [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the studies agree that masks are beneficial, but they also suggest that effectiveness depends on compliance, duration, mask type, and the surrounding environment [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: Based on the provided summaries, nano-enhancers are described as better for workpiece burn mainly because they improve lubrication, cooling, and heat transfer during machining, rather than because of any direct evidence from a workpiece-burn-specific comparison [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. In one machining review, nano-enhancers are recommended for their high thermal conductivity, which is presented as helping solve burn problems, especially in titanium alloy grinding [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also says nano-enhancers with high hardness and spherical characteristics, together with high-viscosity biolubricant, are better for addressing wheel wear and nickel-based alloy surface burn, while low-viscosity biolubricant is suggested for high-strength steel to reduce clogging issues [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review of nano-enhanced biolubricants reports preliminary experimental improvements in tool wear and surface integrity, and attributes their advantage to distinct film-formation, atomization, and infiltration mechanisms that improve lubrication and heat transfer [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. However, that same review also says the overall mechanisms are still indistinct, so the explanation is not yet fully settled [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. Several other summaries do not directly address workpiece burn or nano-enhancers in machining, and instead discuss unrelated topics such as nanotechnology in environmental applications or burn treatment in medicine, which means they cannot support a stronger conclusion here [https://openalex.org/W4322505914||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4375866196||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4324057306||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests nano-enhancers are considered better because they can reduce heat and improve surface integrity under machining conditions, but the provided sources do not establish a universal or fully explained advantage for all materials and processes [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Across the supplied summaries, most papers are broader reviews of sustainable lubrication and do not provide canola-oil-specific experimental evidence for hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) [https://openalex.org/W4327639096||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000]. The clearest direct evidence comes from the canola-oil study, where hBN was used as a solid nano-additive to improve the tribological performance of canola oil, which the paper describes as having lower tribological performance than petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, hBN was tested at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% in canola oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The evaluation focused on dynamic viscosity, boundary-lubrication coefficient of friction (COF), and wear, using a pin-on-disk test [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The best hBN-only result was at 1.0 wt.%, which gave the lowest COF and a 40% reduction compared with base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also reports that combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelet (GNP) in canola oil produced a stronger effect, reducing friction by 56% and wear by 90% relative to base oil, likely because of a protective composite film and polishing mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. More generally, the reviews agree that bio-lubricants and plant-based oils are attractive because of biodegradability, renewability, and low toxicity, but they also note drawbacks such as lower thermo-oxidative stability and higher pour points [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4401870224||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, hBN appears in the evidence primarily as a tribologically functional nano-additive in sustainable lubrication reviews, but the detailed canola-oil evaluation is limited to one study with the measurements and operating conditions described above [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
final_answer: The clearest evidence indicates that, in Romania, the SDG Index is used by calculating progress toward the SDGs at the local and regional level through an integrated approach built on 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. This suggests the index is meant to aggregate multiple measures into a single assessment framework for territorial benchmarking, although the other supplied papers do not provide Romania-specific methodological detail and instead discuss broader indicator-selection or monitoring frameworks [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4389430761||ABSTRACT||001]. The Romanian results reported in the summary show a strongly uneven spatial pattern: the highest sustainable development performance is concentrated in certain specific geographical areas, while rural areas and extended peripheral regions in the east and south perform worst [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. This implies that the SDG Index is being used not just as a national average, but as a way to reveal intra-country disparities and identify lagging territories for policy attention [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the other papers, there is agreement that robust regional SDG monitoring depends on adaptable indicators, benchmarking, and strong data infrastructure, but they do not report Romania-specific outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3122113593||ABSTRACT||001]. The main limitation is that only one supplied summary actually contains Romania-specific SDG Index results, so the evidence base for the local/regional Romanian case is narrow [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
final_answer: Across the evidence, the clearest direct answer is that FTs do add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when acting as boundary spanners, and this is distinguished from merely complying by separating compliance-oriented from improvement-oriented actions [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. That interpretation is shaped by social capital, because the way FTs extend sustainable supply chain initiatives up to sub-tier suppliers depends on the cognitive and relational ties they have with focal firms and with suppliers already in the network [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. More broadly, several papers suggest that sustainability requirements are not fixed or neutral in practice: professionals operationalise sustainability through their own perceptions of balance across environmental, economic, and social dimensions, and these perceptions vary across professional and geographical contexts [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000]. Relatedly, sustainability reporting and standard-setting are described as contested arenas where actors retain their own perspectives, uphold specific interpretations of rules, and negotiate legitimacy, which leaves room for subjective application rather than a single harmonized reading [https://openalex.org/W4225388860||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4410729659||ABSTRACT||001]. The evidence also points to ambiguity in materiality and sustainability standards, with materiality described as contested and sustainability standards shaped by interests rather than purely technical or neutral criteria [https://openalex.org/W4289767614||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313644972||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, some papers do not directly address FT behavior and instead only show that sustainability work benefits from diverse perspectives, intentional practices, or more systematic conceptual models, which means they support the general idea of interpretation but do not specifically explain FT boundary-spanning behavior [https://openalex.org/W4382811259||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3157489939||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4311158026||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the literature suggests that FTs interpret sustainability requirements through their own professional judgments and context, but the strength and direction of that interpretation depend on social relationships, role context, and how clearly the requirements are defined [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4225388860||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the papers, organizational learning capability appears to support radical innovation mainly by creating the internal conditions that allow experimentation, dialogue, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. One study is especially direct: it finds that organizational learning capability fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, making it an explanatory mechanism rather than just a background condition [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. This same paper concludes that organizational learning capability is key to understanding how leadership affects radical innovation and is important for competing in a turbulent context [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||001]. Related evidence from another study suggests that organizational learning strengthens innovation capability and contributes to sustainable value creation, but that paper does not directly examine radical innovation, so its relevance is indirect [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000]. Additional studies also imply that learning-oriented capabilities can support innovative outcomes by improving innovation behavior, knowledge absorption, and the processing of information, though these papers focus on sustainable performance, competitive advantage, or business transformation rather than radical innovation specifically [https://openalex.org/W3211385979||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4320476375||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, the literature suggests that radical, systemic innovations are more likely when low cognitive and low micro-institutional proximity are combined with high organizational, social, or geographical proximity, indicating that organizational learning may help create the proximity and connectedness that support radical change [https://openalex.org/W4392624484||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence points to organizational learning capability as a facilitator of radical innovation through mediation, capability-building, and supportive learning climates, but the direct evidence base is limited and uneven across the studies [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Microplastics in fishmeal threaten global public health mainly by entering aquaculture feeds and then moving into fish that people eat, creating a food-chain pathway for human exposure [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. One study of commercial fish feeds in Bangladesh found all samples contaminated, with mean abundance of 500 to 2200 MPs/kg, and explicitly framed this as a public health concern because farmed fish may carry those particles into human food supplies [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper reports that microplastics are especially concerning because they accumulate in marine organisms used to make fishmeal, can be introduced into aquaculture systems through contaminated feed, and may accumulate in edible fish portions, which the authors say can cause severe physiological disorders in fish consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001]. Additional evidence supports the broader mechanism that microplastics can persist, carry hazardous chemicals such as persistent organic pollutants, and act as a pathway for harmful contaminants in the food chain with serious consequences for human health [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the evidence is largely indirect: the Bangladesh study did not measure human outcomes, and one zebrafish study found altered biochemical markers but no serious toxic effects because internalization was lacking, so the human-health impact remains inferential rather than directly demonstrated [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9967563||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also emphasizes that microplastic detection methods vary widely, making global conclusions difficult and adding uncertainty to estimates of risk from fishmeal contamination [https://openalex.org/W4367322982||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the papers agree that the threat is via contaminated aquatic food chains and seafood consumption, but they differ in how directly they connect fishmeal to proven human harm versus potential risk [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: In men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, elevated FSH is generally associated with a more impaired clinical and laboratory profile, including lower testicular volume and worse spermatogenesis [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. One study also found that the chromosomal-anomaly group had higher mean FSH than the undefined-cause group, together with lower testicular volume and a lower rate of normal spermatogenesis [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. Within these chromosomal anomalies, Klinefelter syndrome (KS) showed the clearest abnormalities, with lower average testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher height and arm span, and higher LH and FSH than the undefined group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Gynecomastia was absent in the undefined-cause group but affected more than half of the KS group, further distinguishing KS from undefined causes [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000]. Testicular XX DSD also showed elevated gonadotropin-related abnormalities, with LH and FSH values intermediate between KS and the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Its penile length was also intermediate, while testicular volume was similar to KS and other clinical data were similar to the undefined group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study supports this overall pattern by reporting that both KS and testicular XX DSD have elevated FSH and more severe testicular dysfunction than the undefined-cause group, although it did not provide detailed numerical comparisons between KS and testicular XX DSD [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. Across studies, elevated FSH appears to track with more severe testicular failure and poorer sperm-production markers in this setting, while KS tends to be the most clinically abnormal subgroup and testicular XX DSD generally falls between KS and undefined causes for several measures [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The supplied evidence links NEDD4 to the IGF1 signaling pathway most directly in gastric cancer cells, where NEDD4 knockdown or overexpression affected tumor growth only in IGF1R-dependent cells and not in IGF1R-independent cells [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. In that study, NEDD4’s effect on Akt activation and tumor growth depended on a PTEN-IRS1 axis, and the authors concluded that NEDD4 promotes proliferation of GC cells dependent on IGF1/IGF1R signaling by antagonizing PTEN’s protein phosphatase activity toward IRS1 [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also reports that NEDD4 is expressed at higher levels in IGF1-high GC tissues than in IGF1-low GC tissues and normal tissues, and that co-high expression of NEDD4 and IGF1 predicts worse prognosis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma study supports the broader idea that NEDD4 can be translationally upregulated and linked to PI3K/AKT signaling through PTEN, but it does not mention IGF1 specifically [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the provided summaries, the strongest evidence therefore places NEDD4 as a pro-growth factor in cells that depend on IGF1/IGF1R signaling, while also suggesting that its translational upregulation can feed into PTEN/AKT-related signaling in other cancer contexts [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. However, several other chunks explicitly do not mention NEDD4 or IGF1, so they do not add support for the linkage and instead underscore that the available evidence is limited to a small number of relevant studies [pmc_PMC9803678||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3199735924||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285014207||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5386455||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386455||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does TSignal handle SPs, and what does it predict about their cleavage site and presence on benchmark datasets?
final_answer: TSignal is described as a deep transformer-based neural network that uses BERT language models and dot-product attention to predict both the presence of signal peptides (SPs) and the cleavage site between the signal peptide and the mature protein [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. In other words, it handles SPs by jointly modeling whether a protein has an SP and where that SP is cleaved [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. On common benchmark datasets, it is reported to achieve competitive accuracy for SP presence prediction [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. The same summary states that it reaches state-of-the-art accuracy for cleavage site prediction for most signal peptide types and organism groups [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. No contradictory evidence is provided in the available summaries, but the evidence base is limited to a single relevant abstract summary [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: Across the papers, textile waste management is consistently framed as moving away from dumping and toward circular systems that prioritize recovery, reprocessing, reuse, recycling, and resource recovery [https://openalex.org/W3205047951||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3206222416||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers emphasize waste conversion as a practical route for turning post-consumer textiles into valuable outputs, such as recycled fiber, purified product streams, glucose, or bio-oil, thereby reducing pollution and dependence on virgin materials [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000]. Biological and enzymatic approaches are repeatedly presented as useful conversion tools, including micro-organisms, enzymes, cellulase hydrolysis, and enzymatic recycling, with some summaries reporting lower energy use than conventional methods [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the evidence shows that conversion is not always straightforward because mixed fibers, finishes, additives, dyes, and finishing chemicals can require pretreatment or can inhibit degradation [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000]. For wastewater derived from textile processing, adsorption is highlighted as a feasible tertiary treatment step for removing dyes and metals, especially because it is cost-effective and depends on the adsorbent used [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. This means adsorption is presented more as a complementary treatment for textile wastewater than as a textile-material conversion pathway itself, since several papers explicitly do not provide evidence on adsorption properties in the waste materials [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3206222416||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the combined picture is that textile waste management can use conversion technologies to create new products and use adsorption-based treatment to polish complex effluents, but no single universally applicable method is identified [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3205047951||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
final_answer:
Across the papers, sustainability reporting is generally portrayed as a way to connect corporate actions to the SDGs, but the strength of that connection varies by context and methodology. One line of evidence argues that sustainability reporting can support SDG implementation by measuring environmental performance and using materiality matrices to incorporate stakeholder views, thereby improving report quality [https://openalex.org/W4200252599||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study similarly presents corporate sustainability reporting, especially under GRI guidelines, as a tool to assess whether SDGs matter to the private sector and how companies contribute to them [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000]. However, this positive framing is complicated by evidence from a large cross-company study showing no correlation in reporting specific SDGs and a disconnect between SDG reporting and actual corporate sustainability performance, suggesting firms may report SDGs arbitrarily rather than based on performance [https://openalex.org/W4394576889||ABSTRACT||000].

From a supply chain perspective, several papers indicate that the reporting-to-SDG link becomes more meaningful when sustainability is assessed across suppliers, value-chain actors, and product life cycles. One study finds that sustainable supply chain management is positively and significantly related to financial performance, SDGs, and the relationship between sustainable supply chains and SDGs, and it explicitly recommends implementing sustainability from supplier to customer to improve operational efficiency and reduce environmental and social impacts [https://openalex.org/W4394886303||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate supply-chain framework paper proposes 91 environmental and social indicators so companies can measure both their own and their suppliers’ sustainability performance while improving transparency and accountability [https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000]. Likewise, another paper argues that SDGs and life-cycle sustainability assessment are complementary, and that linking LCSA to SDGs can improve transparency and consistency in reporting sustainability performance of product systems [https://openalex.org/W4281493513||ABSTRACT||001].

At the same time, the literature repeatedly notes gaps in current SDG reporting practices. In tourism, companies may cite SDGs in reports but still fail to explain how sustainability initiatives shape their contribution to the goals [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000]. A Sri Lankan corporate reporting study found SDG 12 and SDG 15 were most frequently reported and introduced a score index integrating SDGs, but it did not provide supply-chain-specific evidence [https://openalex.org/W4392003298||ABSTRACT||001]. More broadly, one paper says SDGs and LCSA are complementary but there is no harmonized way to link them yet, while another says GRI-based supply-chain indicators are useful for SDG-oriented measurement but does not explicitly treat sustainability reporting as a separate construct [https://openalex.org/W4380365728||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4327714039||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests sustainability reporting matters most when it is tied to concrete performance indicators and supply-chain or life-cycle analysis, but current reporting often remains incomplete, inconsistent, or weakly connected to actual sustainability outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4394576889||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do sustainable technologies, such as clean energy in manufacturing and green and reverse logistics, support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises, and what did the analysis find about enterprise adoption and environmental management?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, sustainable technologies are consistently presented as complementary to Industry 4.0 innovation because they can improve environmental sustainability while supporting industrial performance and growth [https://openalex.org/W4226256571||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001]. Reviews across the literature report that Industry 4.0 technologies can reduce resource consumption, improve manufacturing efficiency, and strengthen sustainability performance in production, supply chains, and delivery chains [https://openalex.org/W4226256571||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001]. In the SDG-oriented review, Industry 4.0 is also linked to sustainable economic growth, innovation, and improved environmental performance, showing that alignment with the SDGs is treated as a pathway to broader sustainability outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4389484631||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001]. The paper on Sustainability 4.0 similarly frames digitisation and sustainability as a combined approach that reduces negative environmental consequences while preserving energy and natural resources, and it places these technologies in manufacturing applications that support environmental sustainability and social inclusion [https://openalex.org/W4282842216||ABSTRACT||001]. Specific to the user’s examples, one study states that clean energy in manufacturing and green/reverse logistics create conditions for industry development and future growth when combined with Industry 4.0 technologies and SDG-based innovation [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. That same Slovakian enterprise study found that more than 82% of the 105 surveyed enterprises implement the SDGs and more than 70% prefer environmental aspects in business management, suggesting substantial but not universal adoption of SDG-oriented practices [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. It also reported a significant relationship between enterprise environmental management in the context of SDGs and sustainability in production and logistics, including a confirmed relationship with renewable energy technology use in the industrial sector [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the literature is not uniformly optimistic, because one review notes that Industry 4.0 technologies can also harm environmental sustainability through pollution, improper waste disposal, and excessive consumption of raw materials, information, and energy [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that sustainable technologies support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth mainly by improving environmental performance, enabling greener production and logistics, and encouraging enterprise-level sustainability practices, but the strength of adoption and management outcomes varies by context and is not fully explained across studies [https://openalex.org/W3170613256||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3120619572||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
final_answer: The systematic review on OSC says that OSC has shown enhanced environmental performance, including reductions in waste generation and carbon emissions, alongside practical benefits such as reduced construction time, lower cost, and improved efficiency [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. It also reports that by 2018, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration, despite these documented benefits [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. This gap between demonstrated environmental gains and limited market uptake makes it timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The review specifically frames this as important because the literature still needs to clarify the learnings, strategies, and critical success factors in both developed and developing regions [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. It further suggests that such clarification would help guide stakeholders in increasing OSC adoption and boosting environmental performance [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the provided summaries, no other paper supplies contradictory OSC-specific evidence, although some unrelated systematic reviews emphasize context dependence and the need for better evaluation methods in sustainability research more generally [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does the study use predictive analytics in the 1-hop work, and what does the 2-hop AI impact assessment say about AI"s role for sustainable development?
final_answer: Across the papers, predictive analytics in the 1-hop work is consistently described as part of AI methods used to forecast, optimize, and monitor sustainability-related systems. One study links predictive modeling to environmental science applications such as climate change, conservation and biodiversity, and sustainable resource management [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000]. Another describes “advanced predictive models and monitoring systems” as improving resource monitoring, agricultural practices, and waste management [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000]. A third paper identifies deep learning and supervised machine learning as the main predictive analytics methods used for forecasting and system optimization in AI-related SDG research [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000], while another associates predictive analytics with machine learning and neural networks for optimizing resources, reducing carbon footprint, and eradicating wastage in cleaner production [https://openalex.org/W4402735735||ABSTRACT||000]. The 2-hop AI impact assessments are also broadly aligned in portraying AI as beneficial for sustainable development, with repeated claims that it can support environmental, economic, and social gains, including climate mitigation, biodiversity protection, cleaner production, efficiency gains, and better resource management [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402735735||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers add that AI can advance the SDGs by enabling data-driven insights and optimizations, and by serving as a central tool in sustainability work [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4405499395||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the assessments are not purely celebratory: they stress that supportive policies and infrastructure are needed to realize AI’s benefits [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000], that AI’s transformative potential is not yet fully realized [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000], and that responsible governance is necessary because AI carries ecological, algorithmic, and socio-economic risks [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000]. Some papers also emphasize the need for transparency, revising AI techniques to make assumptions clearer, and using assessment questions or frameworks to guide more sustainable AI design [https://openalex.org/W4220935479||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4405499395||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests predictive analytics is used as a core forecasting/optimization tool in the 1-hop work, while the 2-hop assessments frame AI as an important enabler of sustainable development whose benefits depend on responsible deployment and governance [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How are the SDOs linked to policy coherance for sustainable development in the EU context?
final_answer: Across the papers, the SDGs are linked to policy coherence for sustainable development in the EU as both a normative framework and an analytical tool for aligning policies across sectors and levels of governance [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies treat coherence as the degree to which EU strategies such as the European Green Deal, the 2030 Agenda, the Circular Economy strategy, and the European Semester Country-Specific Recommendations are co-integrated, with mapping or correlation exercises used to assess alignment [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3209532954||ABSTRACT||000]. In this view, the SDGs help identify whether progress in one area undermines another, and they also provide a basis for monitoring where coherence is weakest, especially in environmental goals [https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also suggests that coherence depends on how implementation tools are designed: Life Cycle Assessment is presented as a way to support policy design and monitoring for SDG and Green Deal ambitions, while the Planetary Boundaries framework adds an absolute sustainability dimension [https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the papers also emphasize that policy coherence is not purely technical; it is shaped by political ideas, institutions, and interests, and depoliticized or “neutral” SDG arrangements may limit transformative change [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000]. Empirically, the EU appears to have incorporated the SDGs into its strategic priorities, but gaps remain because some major challenges are not reflected in the CSRs and environmental goals remain the least coherent [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, the evidence points to a need for a system perspective, better trade-off analysis, and context-specific priorities to strengthen policy coherence across governance levels and scales [https://openalex.org/W4366975340||ABSTRACT||001].
