query: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?
final_answer: Across the supplied studies, the connecting thread is that sustainability in the built environment is treated both as a design/performance goal and as an implementation challenge. The Southern Africa off-site construction study shows that prefabricated construction methods can mainstream sustainability into affordable housing, with better overall sustainability performance for innovative prefabricated construction methods under sustainability-related metrics, including lifecycle energy and cost considerations [https://openalex.org/W4386401188||ABSTRACT||000]. In Ghana, sustainability is framed through environmental performance and residential-building implementation: one study found that environmental indicators across the full building life cycle were all important, especially water quality, air quality, energy use and conservation, and environmental compliance and management [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||001]. A second Ghana study on residential buildings shows that sustainability must be integrated throughout development but is hindered by management, standards, society, and knowledge barriers, with management-related barriers identified as the most significant obstacle to implementation [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001]. This aligns with the Ghana retrofit barrier analysis, which also emphasizes cultural, economic, technical knowledge, and regulatory barriers as obstacles to sustainability in the built environment [https://openalex.org/W4293340752||ABSTRACT||001]. More generally, the barrier-focused papers agree that sustainability progress depends on addressing education, incentives, lifecycle-cost awareness, and policy support rather than relying on technical solutions alone [https://openalex.org/W3145060410||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3132259306||ABSTRACT||000]. In Saudi Arabia, the Mostadam discussion places sustainable residential buildings within a broader Vision 2030 transition toward sustainable buildings and cities, presenting the framework as a pathway to comprehensive sustainable development at both building and city scales [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the evidence suggests that environmental sustainability, sustainable residential buildings, and implementation barriers are interdependent: technical approaches such as off-site construction and rating frameworks like Mostadam define what sustainable buildings can look like, while Ghana- and Iran-based barrier analyses explain why achieving them is difficult in practice [https://openalex.org/W4386401188||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W3132259306||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What did the interviews with retailers and service providers in North America reveal about managing product returns sustainably?
final_answer: Interviews with multichannel retailers, retail experts, and return service providers in the UK and North America found that firms were largely focused on the financial impact of product returns and had little awareness of their environmental impacts [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The interviews also showed that retailers generally lacked a comprehensive approach to managing returns sustainably, indicating that environmental sustainability was not yet integrated into returns management practice [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the study identified barriers that prevented retailers from developing environmental sustainability plans for returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. Based on those findings, the authors proposed strategies to reduce the environmental impact of product returns and developed a framework for environmental sustainability in returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. Related evidence from a separate paper on retail returns supply chains suggests that sustainability hindrances in this area include the need to encourage RE producers to compete and a lack of governmental support for sustainable supply chain solutions [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001]. Other provided papers do not directly address interviews with North American retailers and service providers about returns management, so they do not add direct evidence to this question [https://openalex.org/W4213078357||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4308154031||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285384093||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4396218243||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386820000||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3207246056||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: Across the provided summaries, the clearest screening description for the 87 life cycle assessment studies is that one review searched Scopus for 2017–2023 using the keywords “Sustainability assessment” or “Life cycle assessment” combined with “Internal combustion engine*” or “ICE*,” and then applied careful screening [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. That same review classified the selected studies along six dimensions: sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies including alternative fuels, types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review used PRISMA plus a literature search in scientific databases and an evaluation matrix to classify papers by integrated criteria, but it does not specify the full screening thresholds or exact selection rules [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. In that review, the studies were categorized by method type, including stand-alone LCA, LCC combined with other analyses, and S-LCA, with reported indicator emphasis on global warming potential, eutrophication, human toxicity, and ecotoxicity [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate automotive LCSA review also found that studies were compared by functional units, system boundaries, indicator selection across sustainability pillars, and interpretation of results, suggesting these were important classification dimensions [https://openalex.org/W4393385633||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the summaries consistently note that most papers do not provide a full exclusion list or detailed selection thresholds, so beyond the keyword-based search, PRISMA/evaluation-matrix approach, and broad dimension-based grouping, the exact screening and classification rules are not fully recoverable from the provided evidence [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4393385633||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: In hepatocellular carcinoma, macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was reported to be significantly upregulated in tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line, and its expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 and tumor size [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. siRNA-mediated MIF knockdown inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in an in vivo xenograft model, while not affecting the cell cycle [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. At the protein level, MIF knockdown increased Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax expression, but decreased cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK expression, suggesting a shift away from growth signaling and toward apoptosis-related pathways [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. These findings indicate that MIF supported tumor cell growth and survival in the reported HCC models, and that its suppression had anti-tumor effects on both cell behavior and signaling protein expression [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. No other provided summaries contributed additional direct evidence about MIF in HCC, so the synthesis is based on a single study and should be interpreted cautiously [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, coronary artery calcification (CAC) is consistently associated with worse outcomes, but the exact complications differ by setting. In a review, CAC was linked to higher future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and improved risk prediction when added to global risk models, although no clinical trial has shown that CAC screening improves clinical outcomes or lowers costs [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, higher coronary calcium scores were also used as prognostic markers for mortality, indicating that CAC has broader adverse prognostic significance in this population [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In trauma patients, left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with developing any complication, and more calcified coronary arteries showed a trend toward more complications; CAC was also associated with an adverse discharge condition on the Glasgow Outcome Scale [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, one calcified-lesion registry focused on procedural treatment found good short-term results after orbital atherectomy and reported no primary safety events at 30 days, suggesting that complications may be limited in that specific treated cohort despite severe calcification [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. Several other papers in the set do not address CAC at all, so they cannot be used to infer CAC-related complications in those contexts [pmc_PMC10140970||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10141707||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9806495||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports CAC as a marker of higher-risk or complication-prone disease, but the type of complication, the population studied, and the clinical context strongly influence the observed association [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: The clearest evidence available indicates that serum KAI1 is downregulated and serum VEGF is upregulated in patients with HCC, and that each marker has diagnostic value on its own [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, KAI1 showed an AUC of 0.907, while VEGF showed an AUC of 0.779, suggesting KAI1 was the stronger single marker of the two [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. When the two markers were used together, diagnostic performance improved compared with KAI1 alone, with sensitivity increasing from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy increasing from 83.06% to 84.68% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The combined panel also achieved a negative predictive value of 78.79%, which supports its usefulness as a diagnostic aid [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors conclude that combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF may greatly improve the efficiency of HCC diagnosis and could form a reliable diagnostic marker panel [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the other supplied summaries do not provide additional evidence on KAI1/VEGF diagnostic performance, so the conclusion rests on a single study and cannot be independently corroborated here [pmc_PMC4320626||ABSTRACT||000; pmc_PMC9972107||ABSTRACT||000; pmc_PMC10063275||ABSTRACT||000; pmc_PMC4169601||ABSTRACT||000].

final_answer: Across the DIEP-focused study, the learning curve appears to have improved over time, but the pattern differed by level of analysis and outcome measured [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. However, that second study is not about DIEP reconstruction, so it can only be used as an external example of how learning curves can improve with experience rather than direct evidence for DIEP [pmc_PMC10141185||ABSTRACT||001]. The remaining paper addresses long-term revision patterns after breast reconstruction and does not provide DIEP-specific learning-curve results [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||002]. Overall, the DIEP evidence suggests modest improvement over time, most clearly in shorter hospital stay and in operative time for one surgeon, but not in all measured outcomes [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models help researchers understand adult heart cardiac regeneration because newborn mouse hearts retain a short-lived regenerative capacity after injury, and this system can reveal the molecular mechanisms that underlie regenerative processes [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. These models are used to identify factors that might stimulate endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which could inform new therapies for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the summaries, neonatal cardiomyocyte models are also shown to be useful for dissecting injury-response pathways, such as 11β-HSD1-dependent mitochondrial injury, oxidative stress, and inflammation, with knockdown improving myocardial function and activating AMPK, PGC-1α, and SIRT1 signaling [pmc_PMC10387747||ABSTRACT||001]. Similarly, neonatal rat cardiomyocyte studies of salusin-β show that suppressing this pathway prevents HG-induced oxidative stress, NF-κB activation, and inflammation, and those pathway findings were linked to improved ventricular function in diabetic rats, suggesting neonatal model results can be translated to adult dysfunction [pmc_PMC5386515||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence provided emphasizes injury-response and cardioprotection pathways more than direct demonstrations of regeneration in adult hearts, so the adult-regeneration link is mainly inferential rather than directly proven in these summaries [pmc_PMC10387747||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5386515||ABSTRACT||001]. The neonatal model paper explicitly frames these systems as translational platforms for testing regenerative therapies, while noting that large-animal and human studies may further guide regenerative medicine approaches [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the common message is that neonatal injury models are valuable because they expose developmental and signaling features that are difficult to see in adult hearts and may point to strategies for boosting repair or regeneration [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5386515||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The ClinicalTrials.gov record information available in the summaries identifies the DECISION phase III study as a randomized, double-blind trial in patients with radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, with lenvatinib starting doses of 18 mg/day or 24 mg/day assigned in the study described by one summary [pmc_PMC9972135||ABSTRACT||000]. Another summary describes DECISION as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III study in locally advanced/metastatic RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, designed to assess whether sorafenib improves progression-free survival [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The treatment schedule differed by source: one record summary reports HRQoL assessments at baseline, every 8 weeks until Week 24, then every 16 weeks and at the off-treatment visit, using EQ-5D-3L and FACT-G with completion/compliance, mean change from baseline, and time to first and definitive deterioration as outcomes [pmc_PMC9972135||ABSTRACT||000], while the other reports treatment continuing until progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent, with efficacy every 56 days and safety every 28 days for the first 8 months then every 56 days thereafter [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The primary endpoint reported for the sorafenib DECISION study is progression-free survival, with secondary endpoints including overall survival, time to disease progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetic analysis [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||002]. The trial registration identifiers also differ across the summaries: one gives ClinicalTrials.gov Number NCT02702388 [pmc_PMC9972135||ABSTRACT||002], while the other gives NCT00984282 [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||002]. Several other summaries explicitly state that they do not provide ClinicalTrials.gov record details, so the evidence base is limited to these two partially overlapping descriptions [pmc_PMC5384304||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386727||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386727||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraqi study of 1-day-old imported broiler chicks from Mosul governorate, maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination were assessed in Cobb 500 and Ross 308 flocks using 707 blood samples [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Both strains showed high and fairly uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 performed better overall than Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Specifically, Cobb 500 had a higher antibody-positive rate (100% vs 97.78%), a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), a lower mean CV (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher mean vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60) [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors concluded that both strains had high and uniform titers, but Cobb 500 produced chicks with higher protective titers than Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. No other provided paper offered relevant Newcastle disease data for broiler chicks in Iraq, so the strain comparison rests on this single study [pmc_PMC10141882||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10059746||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC4172590||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the studies, mask mandates and mask use were generally associated with fewer COVID-19 cases or reduced transmission, especially when compliance and other controls were strong [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9482873||ABSTRACT||001]. A U.S. state-level analysis found that mask mandates were more effective in states with higher compliance, and estimated that a national mask mandate starting May 15, 2020 could have lowered total U.S. infections by 23.7% to 30.4% by November 15, 2020 [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. The same study also found that mask mandates could offset about one third of the case-growth increase associated with a one-standard-deviation rise in mobility, suggesting mandates helped blunt transmission when people were moving around more [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate county-level study found that behavioral policies, including face mask mandates, were linked to lower COVID-19 incidence when they were in place for at least 2 months, compared with less than 1 month or no policy [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers support the same direction of effect by reporting that face masks significantly protected healthcare workers from infection, with evidence especially supporting N95 masks, and that surgical masks outperformed cloth masks in healthcare settings [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. Several summaries also emphasize that masks work best when combined with other measures such as social distancing, hand cleanliness, cohorting, and proper ventilation, and that poor pairing with ventilation can reduce effectiveness [pmc_PMC9482873||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4221110503||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the study findings point to masks helping reduce cases, but the effect depends on adherence, type of mask, and whether masks are combined with other interventions [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: Across the machining-focused papers, nano-enhancers are described as better for workpiece burn mainly because they improve heat dissipation, lubrication, and anti-friction behavior during cutting or grinding [pmc_PMC9971250||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper specifically says carbon nanotubes raise thermal conductivity in conventional fluids, which improves heat removal and is linked to better load-carrying capacity and wear resistance, helping explain performance gains in burn-related conditions [pmc_PMC9971250||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review says nano-enhanced biolubricants outperform biolubricant-based MQL because of advanced lubrication and heat-transfer mechanisms, including distinctive film formation, atomization, and infiltration behavior [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. For titanium alloy machining, the literature recommends nano-enhancers because their high thermal conductivity helps solve the “burn puzzle,” and it also notes that high hardness and spherical shape are desirable properties [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. The same source suggests nano-enhancers can be part of a strategy for nickel-based alloy surface burn, alongside high-viscosity biolubricants with high fatty acid saturation, which shows that nano-enhancers are often presented as one component of a broader solution rather than a stand-alone fix [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate review adds that nanofluids are considered promising because of their excellent thermophysical properties, but they are still developmental and need more study to become cost-effective [https://openalex.org/W4294292954||ABSTRACT||001]. That review also notes that alternative methods are not yet mature enough and may underperform in tribological properties, surface finish, cutting forces, and working-fluid consumption, which supports the comparative advantage of nano-enhancers in machining performance [https://openalex.org/W4294292954||ABSTRACT||001]. However, not all provided papers address this question: some summaries discuss sustainability, heat treatment, thermal storage, or nanosphere lithography rather than workpiece burn, so they do not directly support the burn-related conclusion [https://openalex.org/W4322505914||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387413839||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10310747||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9971052||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) played the role of a solid lubricant nano-additive in a canola oil bio-lubricant study, where it was added to canola oil specifically to improve tribological performance because canola oil alone was described as underperforming relative to petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The study tested canola oil with hBN loadings of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% and evaluated the formulations by measuring dynamic viscosity, coefficient of friction (COF), and wear in the boundary lubrication regime using pin-on-disk tests [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. Among those formulations, 1.0 wt.% hBN gave the lowest COF, reported as 40% lower than the base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. query: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
final_answer: The evidence suggests that FT-like boundary-spanning actors often do not simply transmit sustainability requirements unchanged; rather, they frequently interpret and adapt them through their own role, perceptions, and local context [https://openalex.org/W4223934530||ABSTRACT||000]. In one study, directors and middle managers applied sustainability differently depending on organizational role and personal perceptions, producing different meanings across levels and functions and implying that boundary-spanning work includes sensemaking as well as translation [https://openalex.org/W4223934530||ABSTRACT||000]. A related finding shows that middle managers treated sustainability requirements through a department-specific lens and prioritized or adapted practices differently across functions, again indicating practical interpretation during implementation [https://openalex.org/W4396791633||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper argues that organizational sustainability identity is socially constructed through employees’ convictions about core operations and customer collaboration, not mainly through formal controls, which suggests that personal beliefs can shape how sustainability requirements are framed in practice [https://openalex.org/W4285585775||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the literature also emphasizes that sustainability implementation is strengthened by shared ownership, informal communication, and collaborative planning, which can reduce purely individual discretion and align interpretations across stakeholders [https://openalex.org/W3173999974||ABSTRACT||001]. More broadly, sustainability is shown to be interpreted in multiple ways in project management research, reinforcing the idea that there is no single uniform meaning of sustainability requirements [https://openalex.org/W3189889143||ABSTRACT||000]. However, several papers explicitly note that they do not directly study FTs or boundary-spanning roles, so the evidence for FT-specific personal interpretation remains indirect rather than definitive [https://openalex.org/W4309402460||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4410729659||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3173999974||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, organizational learning capability appears to contribute to innovation by creating conditions that support experimentation, dialogue, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment, which the evidence links directly to radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. One study reports that organizational learning capability fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, suggesting it functions as an explanatory pathway rather than a standalone driver [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. A related paper, while not directly studying radical innovation, argues that organizational learning improves how innovation is informed and processed, implying that learning helps make innovation more effective and less disruptive [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from another study similarly indicates that ambidextrous learning in the top management team is positively associated with adoption of sustainable business model innovations, and that diversity and university-industry collaboration strengthen learning that supports innovation [https://openalex.org/W4323928282||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the papers suggest that organizational learning capability contributes to more radical forms of innovation by enabling richer knowledge processing, broader external interaction, and organizational conditions that encourage novel action [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000]. However, several papers in the set do not address organizational learning capability or radical innovation directly, instead discussing related constructs such as knowledge risk management, absorptive capacity, networking, agility, or digital innovation, which limits how far the evidence can be generalized [https://openalex.org/W4285014380||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4403733178||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4320476375||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4394927537||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Across the provided papers, the main public-health concern is that microplastics can enter fishmeal through contaminated marine organisms and then move into aquaculture feed and seafood consumed by people [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. One study specifically reports that commercial fish feeds in Bangladesh were 100% contaminated with microplastics, with measured abundances of 500 to 2200 MPs/kg, supporting a direct contamination route into aquaculture food chains that can affect fish eaten by humans [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. The same paper links several polymer types, including PE, PVC, PP, and PET, to possible health-risk concern and recommends avoiding plastic materials in packaging and storage to reduce contamination [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper argues that once microplastics enter aquaculture through fishmeal, they may interact with pond ecosystems, alter cultured fish physiology and behavior, accumulate in edible portions, and potentially cause severe physiological disorders in consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. Broader reviews agree that microplastics are a global threat because they persist in the environment, are consumed by organisms, can carry hazardous chemicals, and may influence the availability and harmfulness of co-contaminants in the food chain [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4396845947||ABSTRACT||000]. Other summaries also support a general human-health concern by stating that microplastics are already found in animals and humans and warrant monitoring and assessment [https://openalex.org/W4401805195||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, several summaries explicitly note that they do not provide fishmeal-specific evidence or direct causal proof of global public health outcomes, so the strongest supported conclusion is a plausible contamination pathway rather than a fully quantified health impact [https://pmc_PMC9967563||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378527951||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4396845947||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is consistently linked to worse testicular function, including failed sperm retrieval and primary testicular dysfunction [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. In a NOA cohort, elevated serum FSH and LH were associated with failed sperm retrieval, whereas successful retrieval was associated with larger testicular volume and a higher T/LH ratio; multivariate analysis identified serum FSH, T/LH ratio, and bilateral testicular volumes as significant predictors of successful sperm extraction [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000]. In men with NOA and chromosomal anomalies, the Klinefelter syndrome (KS) group had lower testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, and higher height, arm span, LH, and FSH than the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Testicular XX DSD showed an intermediate pattern, with LH, FSH, and penile length between KS and undefined-cause groups, while testicular volume was similar to KS and the remaining data were similar to the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors conclude that clinical and laboratory data can distinguish men with chromosomal anomalies, especially KS and testicular XX DSD, from those with undefined causes or other chromosomal anomalies [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study supports the broader interpretation that elevated FSH reflects primary testicular dysfunction and is useful in identifying chromosomal contexts that should prompt AZF screening, although it does not provide subgroup-level FSH comparisons for KS, testicular XX DSD, or undefined-cause men [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, KS appears more severely affected than testicular XX DSD, which tends to fall between KS and undefined causes for several hormonal and clinical measures [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The strongest evidence links translational regulation of NEDD4 to the IGF1/IGF1R pathway in gastric cancer (GC) cells, where cells were split into IGF1R-dependent and IGF1R-independent groups based on Akt phosphorylation after OSI906 treatment [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000]. In that setting, NEDD4 knockdown or overexpression changed tumor growth only in IGF1R-dependent cells, indicating that NEDD4 functions specifically in the IGF1 signaling context rather than uniformly across all GC cells [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study reports that NEDD4 promotes proliferation in IGF1/IGF1R-dependent cells by antagonizing PTEN protein phosphatase activity toward IRS1, and that a PTEN-IRS1 axis is required for NEDD4-mediated control of Akt activation and tumor growth [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Clinically, NEDD4 is higher in IGF1-high GC tissues than in IGF1-low and normal tissues, and co-high expression of NEDD4 and IGF1 predicts worse prognosis, supporting an association with IGF1-driven disease [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, other provided papers do not address NEDD4 or IGF1 signaling and therefore do not add direct evidence for this link [pmc_PMC9803355||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3199735924||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386737||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9974429||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9732911||ABSTRACT||000]. A related but distinct study in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma does show that NEDD4 is translationally upregulated and that its higher protein expression reflects translational activation, but that work connects NEDD4 to PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling rather than IGF1 specifically [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does TSignal handle SPs, and what does it predict about their cleavage site and presence on benchmark datasets?
final_answer: TSignal is described as a deep transformer-based neural network that combines BERT language models with dot-product attention to predict both whether a protein has a signal peptide (SP) and where the cleavage site lies between the SP and the mature protein [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. It is specifically intended to handle SPs despite their variable length, lack of conserved motifs, and sensitivity to mutations [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. On common benchmark datasets, TSignal is reported to achieve competitive accuracy for SP presence prediction [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. The same summary states that it reaches state-of-the-art cleavage site prediction for most SP types and organism groups on those benchmarks [pmc_PMC10311348||ABSTRACT||000]. No other provided paper summary offers additional TSignal-specific evidence, so the benchmark and performance claims rely entirely on this source [pmc_PMC4176846||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9883675||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: Textile waste management can use waste conversion to turn biomass and textile-related residues into adsorbent materials that treat wastewater while also creating reusable products from the waste stream [https://openalex.org/W4362593051||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3137350553||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the papers, biochar and biosorbents are repeatedly identified as the main conversion products because they are low-cost, sustainable, and can remove dyes, heavy metals, and other refractory pollutants through adsorption [https://openalex.org/W4388723729||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4317934337||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4362576918||ABSTRACT||000]. Their adsorption performance is linked to properties such as porosity, surface area, surface charge, functional groups, pore structure, and accessible sorption sites, which can be improved by thermal, mechanical, chemical, or other functionalization methods [https://openalex.org/W4317934337||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285043499||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392817207||ABSTRACT||000]. Specific examples show that waste conversion can yield effective textile-wastewater adsorbents: orange peel powder mixed with biochar removed COD, TDS, turbidity, and color within 30 minutes, while areca nut husk biochar removed Rhodamine B and Alizarine red S with 89% and 87% dye removal in 40 minutes [https://openalex.org/W4362593051||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4389010096||ABSTRACT||000]. Cotton waste can likewise be processed into functional biomaterials and cellulose nanocrystals, and surface modification increases its adsorption of dyes and heavy metals [https://openalex.org/W3137350553||ABSTRACT||000]. The papers also agree that reusability is important: spent adsorbents can be regenerated, reused, or converted again through routes such as co-digestion and pyrolysis, supporting a circular waste-management approach [https://openalex.org/W4362593051||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4410456021||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285043499||ABSTRACT||000]. However, one review notes that waste-derived adsorbents are often more suitable for cationic dyes than anionic dyes, so modification is often needed for broader dye removal [https://openalex.org/W4295006283||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that textile waste management can exploit waste conversion to produce adsorbents, use their adsorption properties for pollutant removal, and then regenerate or repurpose the spent materials to reduce disposal burdens and secondary waste [https://openalex.org/W4388723729||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4317934337||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4362593051||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
final_answer: Across the papers, sustainability reporting is consistently framed as a transparency and accountability tool that can communicate sustainability performance to stakeholders and support better measurement through standardized indicators and reporting frameworks [https://openalex.org/W4402984150||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4396752316||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies link reporting to sustainability outcomes through ESG disclosure, with evidence that ESG performance, stakeholder engagement, and standalone sustainability reports positively influence firm-level SDG disclosure [https://openalex.org/W4389274682||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper directly asks whether SDG disclosure reflects underlying corporate sustainability performance and notes that this relationship remains unclear in the prior literature, even while studying ESG performance and SDG disclosure across 635 firms in 45 countries [https://openalex.org/W4388289542||ABSTRACT||000]. In contrast, another paper argues sustainability reporting is not very useful for tracking sustainability performance or comparing firms over time because it functions mainly as a transparency regulation instrument and lacks aggregate measures or accruals [https://openalex.org/W4379261092||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, other papers are more optimistic, suggesting sustainability reporting can improve disclosure quality, stakeholder communication, and continuous performance improvement, especially when supported by integrated reporting, ESG accounting, or clearer disclosure formats [https://openalex.org/W4402984150||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4390695027||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4294740915||ABSTRACT||000]. On the supply chain side, the evidence shows that reporting can matter through value-chain and supplier information: one paper states sustainability reporting includes information about firms in the value chain, while another develops a supply-chain sustainability assessment framework that lets companies measure both their own and suppliers’ environmental and social performance [https://openalex.org/W4379261092||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000]. This suggests that the supply chain framework is relevant, but mainly as a measurement and transparency context rather than as direct proof that reporting always improves sustainability performance [https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4379261092||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the papers support a conditional conclusion: sustainability reporting can be linked to SDG disclosure and sustainability performance, especially when it uses robust metrics, stakeholder engagement, and supply-chain indicators, but the strength of that link is contested and not uniformly supported across studies [https://openalex.org/W4389274682||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4388289542||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4379261092||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
final_answer: For the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, one study explicitly compared five MCDA methods: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA, using eight criteria across 12 district heating companies [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The study’s sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in three ways: changing them individually to determine stability ranges, changing them individually by a fixed amount to see effects on average scores, and comparing AHP weights with equal weights [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Its main conclusion was that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analyses of district heating systems, but they differ in calculation process and in how results are interpreted [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. This indicates agreement on overall suitability while still highlighting methodological differences that can affect practical use [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. A related district-heating sustainability study used fuzzy AHP with fuzzy TOPSIS and reported that an 18-scenario sensitivity analysis supported the reliability and stability of the ranking results under changed sub-criteria weights [https://openalex.org/W4365453722||ABSTRACT||001]. Although that study did not compare multiple MCDA methods beyond the fuzzy AHP–fuzzy TOPSIS framework, it reinforces the broader finding that weight sensitivity is important for judging robustness in sustainability rankings [https://openalex.org/W4365453722||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from broader sustainability reviews also suggests growing use of hybrid MCDM approaches and ongoing concerns about subjective weight assignment and model uncertainty, which helps explain why sensitivity analysis is central in these assessments [https://openalex.org/W4407409800||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do the sustainability ideas in the supply chain management framework and the article on sustainable marketing both show how environmental sustainability can be advanced and linked to company image?
final_answer: Across the papers, sustainability is presented as something companies advance by embedding it into concrete business practices rather than treating it as a symbolic claim. In the supply chain management framework, environmental sustainability is strengthened through customer relationships, postponement, information sharing, and information quality, and these practices can also improve financial performance and help managers strengthen sustainability in manufacturing companies [https://openalex.org/W3132273715||ABSTRACT||001]. A related supply-chain/strategy perspective says sustainability becomes more effective when it is built into business strategy, where consumer, supplier, and employee engagement, reduced risk, and better operational management support broader company performance [https://openalex.org/W3135028795||ABSTRACT||002]. The more strategic supply-chain framework also argues that employees’ motivation and managerial attitude shape strategic sustainability orientation, which then works through corporate environmental management and corporate social responsibility to improve firm performance [https://openalex.org/W3128290205||ABSTRACT||000]. The sustainable marketing papers show a similar logic: companies advance environmental sustainability by reducing environmental impact, using sustainable practices, offering eco-friendly products, adapting marketing to consumer demands, and communicating sustainability transparently [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4396847081||ABSTRACT||000]. These marketing studies also make the company-image link explicit by showing that sustainability helps build customer trust, reputation, loyalty, competitive advantage, and stronger brand image [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4392716256||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4401289024||ABSTRACT||000]. One important contrast is that the supply-chain summaries emphasize operational and performance mechanisms, while the marketing summaries focus more directly on consumer perceptions, brand/reputation, and market differentiation [https://openalex.org/W3132273715||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3135028795||ABSTRACT||002] [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001]. A further warning from the evidence is that sustainability must be implemented visibly: one paper reports that sustainability orientation can hurt brand image if it is not backed by action, creating greenwashing concerns, whereas actual implementation improves brand image [https://openalex.org/W4408946628||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the papers agree that environmental sustainability is advanced through concrete organizational practices and that company image improves when those practices are visible, credible, and tied to responsibility [https://openalex.org/W3128290205||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408946628||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do sustainable technologies, such as clean energy in manufacturing and green and reverse logistics, support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises, and what did the analysis find about enterprise adoption and environmental management?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, sustainable technologies are consistently presented as enablers of Industry 4.0-driven innovation and SDG-oriented growth in industrial enterprises, especially when digital tools are linked to environmental goals [https://openalex.org/W4392974914||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4389484631||ABSTRACT||000]. One review argues that Industry 4.0 applications can improve supply-chain optimization, traceability, waste reduction, and resource management, thereby reducing environmental impact and supporting a broader sustainability transition [https://openalex.org/W4392974914||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper specifically connects clean energy in manufacturing and green/reverse logistics to Industry 4.0-enabled sustainable innovation, stating that these functions strengthen green process innovation capacity and the ability to develop or adopt sustainable technologies [https://openalex.org/W3189862204||ABSTRACT||000]. The Slovakia-based enterprise study provides empirical support for this linkage, reporting that more than 82% of 105 surveyed enterprises implement the SDGs and more than 70% prioritize environmental aspects in business management, with significant relationships found between environmental management in the context of SDGs and sustainability in production and logistics [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. It also found a statistically confirmed relationship between renewable energy technology use in industry and sustainability in logistics, which directly supports the query’s focus on clean energy and logistics-based sustainability [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the literature is not uniformly optimistic: one review notes negative environmental effects from Industry 4.0 systems, including air pollution, improper waste disposal, and excessive consumption of raw materials, information, and energy, suggesting a gap between intended and actual sustainable production [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that enterprise adoption of Industry 4.0 and sustainable technologies can improve environmental and organizational performance, but the benefits depend on how well firms integrate sustainability into management, logistics, and innovation practices [https://openalex.org/W4327944862||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001].

query: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
final_answer: The supplied summaries do not provide a single paper that explicitly answers all parts of the question about OSC, but they do support a partial synthesis. Across the OSC-focused reviews, the environmental emphasis is consistent: sustainability should be built into materials selection, processing, device architectures, recycling, and end-of-life management, with attention to environmental effects across synthesis, processing, and recycling rather than performance alone [https://openalex.org/W4381189818||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3215603632||ABSTRACT||001]. One review also frames natural materials for OSC as abundant, low-cost, degradable, and renewable, highlighting their promise for low-cost and green manufacturing [https://openalex.org/W4319844552||ABSTRACT||000]. The broader photovoltaic literature in the provided summaries agrees that life-cycle and recycling-oriented approaches are central to improving environmental performance, and one review states directly that solar electricity has much lower impacts than fossil fuel electricity in all categories [https://openalex.org/W4307573405||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400414139||ABSTRACT||001]. On market context, the clearest evidence from the OSC-related summaries is that organic electronic applications were gaining momentum and that OLED displays had a market size of over $25 billion, helping build an ecosystem for other applications, but none of the excerpts explicitly states OSC market penetration by 2018 [https://openalex.org/W4381189818||ABSTRACT||000]. Because the provided evidence does not include the specific systematic-review conclusion on OSC’s 2018 penetration, the exact environmental-performance comparison for OSC, or the review’s stated rationale for why it is timely to identify the factors behind improved performance in developed and developing regions, those elements cannot be recovered from the supplied chunks alone [https://openalex.org/W3215603632||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4319844552||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4413108186||ABSTRACT||000]. What can be said is that the summaries collectively portray OSC/organic electronics as at a critical sustainability juncture, with growing markets and a need to align performance, environmental benefits, and circularity [https://openalex.org/W4381189818||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3215603632||ABSTRACT||001].

key_claims.notes: The cited abstract explicitly says sustainability should be built into materials selection, processing, device architectures, recycling, and end-of-life, and that materials choices should consider environmental effects as well as performance.

query: How does the study use predictive analytics in the 1-hop work, and what does the 2-hop AI impact assessment say about AI"s role for sustainable development?
final_answer: Across the supplied studies, the 1-hop work uses predictive analytics mainly as a forecasting and optimization tool: one paper says it forecasts future environmental impacts from historical data so companies can take proactive measures to reduce harm, while also using AI/ML/NLP to process heterogeneous inputs such as IoT sensors, satellite imagery, and corporate disclosures for environmental assessment and reporting [https://openalex.org/W4399702720||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper describes predictive models and monitoring systems as improving resource monitoring, agricultural optimization, and waste management, and a third says deep learning and supervised machine learning are the most prominently applied algorithms for forecasting and system optimization in AI-related SDG research [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000]. One study further reports that an explainable AI predictive model outperforms traditional methods and supports sustainable energy management and Net Zero alignment, indicating that predictive analytics is being used not just for prediction but for practical sustainability decision support [https://openalex.org/W4404798080||ABSTRACT||000]. The 2-hop AI impact assessments are broadly optimistic about AI’s role for sustainable development, describing it as significant or transformative for sustainability, environmental accounting, urban development, and SDG implementation [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4399702720||ABSTRACT||003; https://openalex.org/W4397008103||ABSTRACT||002]. Several papers emphasize that AI can provide data-driven insights, enhanced transparency, real-time monitoring, and environmental, economic, and social benefits, including climate mitigation and biodiversity support [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4399702720||ABSTRACT||003; https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the assessments are conditional rather than unconditional: they stress the need for supportive policies, infrastructure, continuous model refinement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and responsible governance to realize benefits [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4399702720||ABSTRACT||003; https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000]. There is also some nuance in how strongly positive the 2-hop assessments are, ranging from strong consensus that AI positively affects most SDGs to more cautious framing that its full potential remains unrealized and that only a few studies combine advanced AI with deep sustainability expertise [https://openalex.org/W4396674183||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How are the SDOs linked to policy coherance for sustainable development in the EU context?
final_answer: Across the reviewed papers, the SDGs are presented as an organizing framework for policy coherence for sustainable development in the EU, but not as a guarantee of coherent action [https://openalex.org/W4412423688||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4391173571||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies describe coherence as essential to the 2030 Agenda because it helps ensure one goal is not achieved at the expense of another and because the Agenda explicitly calls for policy and institutional coherence [https://openalex.org/W4412423688||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000]. In the EU context, this coherence is linked to integrating SDGs into strategic frameworks for sustainable and inclusive growth and to using regional indicators and monitoring systems to align policies with local realities [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||000]. Evidence also suggests that SDG interactions matter empirically: EU countries’ progress is negatively associated with trade-offs and positively associated with synergies among indicators, implying that reducing conflicts and strengthening complementarities can improve coherence and progress [https://openalex.org/W4205096557||ABSTRACT||000]. However, multiple papers warn that coherence is limited by politics, institutions, and uneven uptake; one study argues that technocratic coordination can mask political struggles, while another finds SDG implementation is often patchy and sometimes symbolic [https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4391173571||ABSTRACT||000]. The EU literature also identifies environmental goals as especially complex and least coherent, with calls to strengthen coherence within biodiversity and climate SDGs and improve data availability for monitoring [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, analytical tools such as LCA are described as pivotal for policy design and monitoring because they can strengthen EU policies toward the SDGs and planetary limits, although the interlinkages between policy, SDGs, and planetary boundaries are uneven across frameworks [https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the papers agree that SDGs can support policy coherence in the EU only when they are backed by robust monitoring, multi-level and multi-actor integration, and attention to the political drivers of implementation rather than purely technical coordination [https://openalex.org/W4381802338||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000].

key_claims.notes: The cited chunks explicitly describe the SDGs as an overarching framework that includes policy and institutional coherence, while also noting that implementation is political, partial, and not guaranteed.

query: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, environmental sustainability is treated as a practical building-performance goal, not just a broad aspiration. In the off-site construction review, OSC is described as offering environmental savings, including reductions in waste generation and carbon emissions, alongside lower time and cost and improved efficiency [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The Ghana studies reinforce that sustainability is assessed through concrete environmental indicators such as water quality, air quality, energy use and conservation, and environmental compliance and management, and they conclude that these indicators are important for evaluating project sustainability [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||001]. The Ghana barrier-analysis paper adds that sustainable construction must be integrated throughout development, but that implementation is constrained by four barrier groups—management, standards, society, and knowledge—with management-related barriers emerging as most significant [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001]. This aligns with the off-site construction review’s emphasis that recognized environmental benefits do not automatically translate into market penetration, so identifying success factors and barriers remains necessary [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The Saudi Arabia Mostadam paper connects sustainability to sustainable residential buildings by tying them to Vision 2030 and emphasizing lower energy use, improved building efficiency, and reduced greenhouse gas emissions [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the themes connect through a common message: sustainable building outcomes depend on both environmentally oriented design/assessment and the ability to implement those ideas through policy, management, and structured frameworks such as Mostadam [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001]. The broader evidence also highlights that sustainability-related gains include cost savings, improved efficiency, and ecosystem or social benefits, but these gains are limited by barriers such as weak knowledge, weak economies, and high construction costs [https://openalex.org/W4313897987||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200347964||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What did the interviews with retailers and service providers in North America reveal about managing product returns sustainably?
final_answer: Interviews with multichannel retailers, retail experts, and return service providers in the UK and North America found that retailers were focusing mainly on the financial impact of returns while having little awareness of their environmental impact and no comprehensive sustainable approach to returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The interviews suggested that managing returns sustainably requires first identifying the barriers that prevent retailers from making environmental sustainability plans for returns and then applying strategies and a framework to reduce the environmental impact of returns [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. A key finding across the interview-based evidence is that reuse can reduce waste and be economically viable, but it is constrained by weak consumer incentives [https://openalex.org/W4403242376||ABSTRACT||001]. Recycling was described as promising, yet limited by technological and awareness barriers, while repair could extend garment life and reduce new production but was restricted by service accessibility and consumer knowledge [https://openalex.org/W4403242376||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the interviews pointed to the need for broader circular-economy changes, including better materials, supportive policies, and shifts in both consumer behavior and corporate practices [https://openalex.org/W4403242376||ABSTRACT||001]. More generally, the reverse-logistics literature in the summaries also emphasizes that a lack of strategic returns planning and poor visibility for recycling and reuse hinder sustainability, whereas strategic planning and visibility can improve sustainability, lower costs, and support a circular economy [https://openalex.org/W4401662603||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4401662603||ABSTRACT||001].

key_claims.claim: Retailers interviewed in the UK and North America paid attention to the financial impact of returns but had little awareness of their environmental impact and lacked a comprehensive sustainable approach to returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001].
key_claims.notes: The cited abstract explicitly says retailers had started paying attention to the financial impact of returns, had little awareness of environmental impacts, and lacked a comprehensive approach.

query: What were the exact biomass yields, nutrient uptake values, and statistical differences among cover crops at each site and year?
final_answer: The provided summaries do not contain the exact biomass yields, nutrient uptake values, or site-by-site/year-by-year statistical comparisons requested for cover crops in general, so those precise figures cannot be reconstructed from the available evidence [https://openalex.org/W4408217859||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390342199||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3129243838||ABSTRACT||000]. One study reports only aggregate effects from a global meta-analysis, finding that legume cover crops increased crop yield by 16.0%, while non-legumes increased soil organic carbon by 4.0% and legumes by 5.9%, and legumes also raised N2O emissions by 36.2% [https://openalex.org/W4408217859||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study on cover crops in soybean systems reports relative, not exact, biomass patterns: on a 3-year average, Pennisetum glaucum and Urochloa brizantha cv. Marandu had the highest biomass, and at one site P. glaucum produced 210% more biomass than the other cover crops [https://openalex.org/W4390342199||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study states that tropical grasses and a cover crop mixture were intermediate in biomass at the higher-biomass site and were not different from P. glaucum at the other site, but it does not provide the statistical test outputs, p-values, or exact year-by-year values [https://openalex.org/W4390342199||ABSTRACT||001]. Nutrient uptake is also described only qualitatively: cover crops differed by species, and Crotalaria spectabilis decomposed rapidly and released substantial nutrients, especially nitrogen, without exact uptake measurements [https://openalex.org/W4390342199||ABSTRACT||001]. Separate wheat studies in the summaries do show treatment effects on biomass and nitrogen status, but they concern inoculation or fertilizer levels rather than cover-crop comparisons by site and year; for example, A. brasilense inoculation increased root and shoot biomass, agronomic efficiency, apparent N-fertilizer recovery, and N uptake, with a 10.3% yield increase [https://openalex.org/W4213363004||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4213363004||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports that cover crop performance varies by species, site, and year, but the supplied chunks do not include the exact numerical biomass, nutrient uptake, or statistical comparison data needed to answer the question precisely [https://openalex.org/W4390342199||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4310861847||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?

Small interfering RNA-mediated knockdown of MIF inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in an in vivo xenograft model, although it did not affect the cell cycle in these cells [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, coronary artery calcification is generally associated with worse outcomes and more complications, but the strength and context of that association vary by population. In level-1 trauma patients, coronary artery calcification on routine CT was independently associated with in-hospital complications, and left main coronary artery calcification was specifically associated with any complication; a greater number of calcified coronary arteries also trended toward complications and was significantly associated with adverse discharge condition [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, coronary artery calcification measures predicted mortality in both women and men over a median 4.4 years, although MESA percentile measures did not outperform absolute coronary artery calcium score [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. A broader review also found that CAC is associated with future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and can improve risk prediction, but it noted that similar CAC levels may correspond to different absolute risk across regions and ethnic groups [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the same review emphasized that no clinical trial has shown whether CAC screening improves clinical outcomes or healthcare costs, so the effect on complications in practice remains uncertain [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. Evidence from another calcification setting showed that higher arterial calcification levels were associated with cardiovascular events, mortality, and limb amputations in hemodialysis patients, supporting the idea that calcification burden can track with adverse events beyond the coronaries [pmc_PMC9967859||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, two papers provided no direct evidence linking coronary artery calcifications to complications, underscoring that not all available texts address the question directly [pmc_PMC10141707||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10140970||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
final_answer: Across the available summaries, the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction appears to improve over time, but the strength of that improvement varies by setting and outcome measured [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. In the institution-wide analysis, later cases had shorter hospital stays than early cases for both single and double DIEP reconstructions, although other outcomes did not differ significantly from the start to the end of the study, suggesting only a modest center-level learning effect [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. By contrast, the single-surgeon analysis showed a clearer learning curve, with a significant reduction in total surgery time over time, implying that individual microsurgeon experience may drive more visible gains than aggregate institutional performance [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. The study therefore characterizes the curve as modest at the center level but more pronounced at the individual level, mainly through shorter operative time and shorter hospitalization in later cases [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. Another summary does not provide DIEP-specific learning-curve metrics and instead compares longer-term revision and secondary reconstruction rates across procedure groups, so it cannot meaningfully describe temporal change in DIEP learning within that study [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests incremental improvement over time rather than a dramatic shift, but the available summaries do not provide enough detail to quantify the trajectory beyond these operative and hospitalization trends [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models are presented as useful because newborn mice retain a brief period of full regenerative capacity after cardiac injury, making them a window into the molecular mechanisms that support heart regeneration [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. These models are described as helping identify factors that can stimulate regeneration by inducing endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which is specifically framed as a way to inform therapeutic strategies for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also suggests that findings from large animal models and humans may further guide regenerative medicine approaches for adult heart repair, indicating that neonatal models are one part of a broader translational pathway rather than a complete answer on their own [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. In contrast, the other provided papers focus on adult injury, endothelial repair responses, or cardiac hypertrophy and do not supply direct evidence about neonatal models or their role in regeneration, limiting cross-paper confirmation of the neonatal-to-adult inference [pmc_PMC10149391||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9283358||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9887753||ABSTRACT||000]. One paper on adult ischemia/reperfusion injury instead illustrates a cardioprotection framework in adults, showing reduced contractile dysfunction, infarct area, apoptosis, and oxidative stress with MK-886, but it does not address neonatal regenerative biology [pmc_PMC10149391||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper emphasizes that endothelial cells support repair and regeneration after myocardial injury by restoring oxygen and nutrient supply and showing transient adaptive changes, which may complement neonatal-model insights but is not itself evidence about neonatal regeneration [pmc_PMC9283358||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports the idea that neonatal injury models are valuable for discovering regeneration-promoting mechanisms that could inspire adult heart therapies, but the provided summaries do not show direct experimental proof that neonatal findings successfully translate to adult cardiac regeneration [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The evidence indicates that the DECISION phase III study was described in one source as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in patients with locally advanced/metastatic RAI-refractory DTC, with ClinicalTrials.gov registration number NCT00984282 [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. In that description, treatment was continued until radiographically documented disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days (2 cycles), while safety assessments were done every 28 days (1 cycle) for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. The same source states that the primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, time to disease progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetic analysis [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. A different paper only confirms that the ClinicalTrials.gov record identifies the study by NCT02709408 and notes that any formal presentation or publication would be handled as a joint publication under ICMJE authorship recommendations [pmc_PMC5387979||ABSTRACT||002]. However, other summaries provided do not supply additional ClinicalTrials.gov details for the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, or endpoints, and one explicitly states that such details are not present in the evidence it reviewed [pmc_PMC9806002||ABSTRACT||001]. Because the summaries report different registration identifiers for what is labeled the DECISION phase III study, the record details appear inconsistent across sources and should be interpreted cautiously [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001; pmc_PMC5387979||ABSTRACT||002].

query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraq study from Nineveh governorate, broiler chicks of both imported strains showed high maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease, with all Cobb 500 chicks positive for maternal antibodies and 97.78% of Ross 308 chicks positive [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The study also found that Cobb 500 had a higher mean maternal antibody titer than Ross 308 (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), a lower CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60) [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors concluded that both strains produced high and uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 produced chicks with higher protective titers than Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. The comparison was based on 1-day-old imported Cobb 500 and Ross 308 broiler chicks sampled from 28 Ross flocks and 17 Cobb flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. No other provided paper summary addressed this specific Iraq/Newcastle disease question, so the Cobb 500 result is the relevant finding here [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10059746||ABSTRACT||000].
