query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the studies, mask use and mask mandates are consistently associated with lower COVID-19 transmission, but the evidence is strongest in specific settings and under certain conditions [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. In healthcare workers, systematic reviews found that PPE use, especially facial masks, provided significant protection against COVID-19 infection, with surgical masks appearing better than cloth masks and N95 masks highlighted as particularly helpful [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||001]. In a US state-level study, mask mandates were estimated to offset about one third of the increase in case growth associated with higher mobility, and stronger effects were seen in states with higher compliance [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. That study also estimated that, had a national mask mandate been enacted on May 15, 2020, total US infections on November 15, 2020 would have been 23.7% to 30.4% lower [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study found that prevention measures lasting at least 2 months were linked to lower incidence than measures lasting less than 1 month, and mask mandates lasting at least 2 months were associated with reductions in monthly incidence ranging from 4 fewer cases per 100,000 in low-vulnerability counties to 401 fewer in high-vulnerability counties [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. One modeling paper also suggested that a face mask used together with upward ventilation could reduce indoor infectious concentration by nearly 99.95% compared with doing nothing [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence is not entirely uniform: one review found the benefits of powered air-purifying respirators, gowns, gloves, and face shields unclear, and another paper warned that masks can be counterproductive if used inappropriately with ventilation [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the studies support mask mandates as a useful non-pharmaceutical intervention for reducing COVID-19 cases, especially when compliance is high, the mandate is maintained longer, and it is paired with appropriate environmental controls [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: Nano-enhancers are presented as useful for workpiece burn control mainly because they improve thermal management and lubrication during machining, which can reduce surface burn and related defects [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. One review says nano-enhancers with high thermal conductivity are recommended because they help solve the workpiece “burn puzzle,” especially for titanium alloy, and that high hardness and spherical characteristics are better because they improve grinding performance [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review describes nano-enhanced biolubricants as improving tribological, thermal, and machined-surface quality through advanced lubrication and heat transfer, with anti-friction effects and distinctive film formation, atomization, and infiltration mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. These papers agree that the appeal of nano-enhancers is largely their thermophysical and interfacial effects, which are framed as superior to conventional fluids for reducing wheel wear, surface burn, and tool wear [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. A broader machining review also calls nanofluids an emerging technology because of their excellent thermophysical properties, but notes that alternative methods are not yet mature and that nanofluids remain developmental and need more detailed, cost-effective study [https://openalex.org/W4294292954||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence is not fully settled: one abstract emphasizes that the overall action of nano-enhanced biolubricants is still indistinct and depends on concentration and dispersion, so the benefits are not described as universal or fully understood [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. Outside machining, related summaries only show that nanoparticles can improve material performance indirectly by improving microstructure or dispersion, but they do not directly explain workpiece burn behavior [https://pmc_PMC5512519||ABSTRACT||000][https://https://openalex.org/W4409451850||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) played a direct additive role in one study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, where it was used as a solid lubricant nano-additive to improve canola oil’s tribological performance because canola oil alone was described as weaker tribologically than petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The evaluation tested canola oil containing 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% hBN nanoparticles and measured dynamic viscosity, coefficient of friction (COF), and wear in the boundary lubrication regime using pin-on-disk tests [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, 1.0 wt.% hBN gave the lowest COF, reported as 40% lower than base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The paper also found that combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelet (GNP) in three nano-lubricant formulations produced a positive synergy, reducing friction by 56% and wear by 90% relative to base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The improvements were attributed to a composite protective film and polishing mechanisms on interacting surfaces [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. Other reviewed papers in the set discuss hBN, plant-based oils, and bio-lubricants more broadly, but they do not provide canola-oil-specific experimental details or additional evaluation conditions for hBN in canola oil [https://openalex.org/W4306936325||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4401870224||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
final_answer: In Romania, the SDG Index is used as a composite measure to assess progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals at local and regional level, based on an integrated approach using 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. A related Romania-focused study used the SDG Index in a simulation model to estimate how local and regional progress could evolve by 2030 and to identify a cost-effective path for each SDG in each city [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001]. That simulation suggested that cities could achieve 9–13 more SDGs by 2030, and that the overall SDG Index could rise from 74.57 to 97.49 if more intensive path adjustment were adopted [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001]. The Romanian local and regional results also showed strong spatial unevenness, with the highest sustainable development performances concentrated in specific geographical areas [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. By contrast, rural areas and extended peripheral regions in the eastern and southern parts of Romania were the poorest performers [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, other papers in the set support the use of SDG-based composite or regional monitoring frameworks for benchmarking and localized assessment, emphasizing that such tools can reveal area-specific strengths and weaknesses and support tailored policy action [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390511697||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence also suggests an important limitation of index-based monitoring: aggregate SDG index values can conceal divergent subregional trends, since an overall increase may hide declines in some subregions [https://openalex.org/W4206568419||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
final_answer: The clearest direct evidence comes from the first-tier supplier study, which finds that FTs can add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements in their boundary-spanning role, especially in how they act upstream with second-tier suppliers [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||000]. That study further shows that FT behavior is not uniform: downstream cognitive and relational social capital with the focal firm shapes whether boundary-spanning actions are compliance-oriented or improvement-oriented [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. Several other papers support the broader idea that sustainability requirements are interpreted and operationalized rather than followed mechanically, such as the EU reporting paper on materiality and reporting processes, and the study suggesting companies may respond to mandatory reporting with more than simple compliance [https://openalex.org/W4200419329||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4214573128||ABSTRACT||001]. Related evidence also shows that professionals’ understandings of sustainability differ across professional and geographical contexts, implying that subjective perspectives can shape how requirements are applied [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, multiple papers do not directly address FTs or their personal interpretation, instead emphasizing collaborative, multi-actor sustainability implementation, boundary-tool-supported negotiation, or leadership and organizational values [https://openalex.org/W3196350704||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3198948227||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4409240686||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that FT interpretation is real but conditional: it emerges in practice, is shaped by relational context, and can tilt toward either compliance or improvement, rather than being a purely standardized response [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the provided papers, organizational learning capability (OLC) appears to contribute to radical innovation mainly by creating conditions that support experimentation, dialogue, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. In the strongest direct evidence, OLC fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, indicating that leader behavior affects radical innovation through the learning capability it helps build [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. This suggests that OLC is not just a background condition but an explanatory mechanism that enables leaders to translate their behavior into radical innovation outcomes [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. Other studies support a broader pattern in which organizational learning improves innovation-related outcomes: one paper reports that organizational learning positively influences innovation capability and partially mediates the relationship between CSR and sustainable value creation [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000], while another links organizational learning to improved performance and suggests that innovation can become disruptive if it is not well-informed and well-processed [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, these findings imply that OLC helps radical innovation by strengthening firms’ capacity to learn, process information, and convert inputs from the environment into innovation-relevant capability [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000]. However, several summaries do not address radical innovation directly and instead focus on sustainability, environmental performance, or transformation, so the evidence is partly indirect [https://openalex.org/W4393229185||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3211385979||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4327722641||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper indicates that radical, systemic innovations are associated with specific proximity conditions rather than organizational learning capability itself, which means the direct role of OLC in radical innovation is not universally established across the evidence base [https://openalex.org/W4392624484||ABSTRACT||001].

final_answer: Across the provided paper summaries, there is no supported identification of a predator as *Puma concolor* in any of the contexts examined [pmc_PMC10065295||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9975479||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC3160898||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10141043||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5381760||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4207033663||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10140996||ABSTRACT||000]. query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Microplastics in fishmeal are described in several summaries as a potential global public health threat because contaminated fishmeal can be used in aquaculture and livestock feeds, allowing microplastics to enter aquaculture systems and potentially accumulate in cultured fish that people consume [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. One review goes further and states that microplastics may accumulate in the edible portions of cultured fish, creating human exposure that may cause severe physiological disorders and thus pose a significant threat to global public health [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001]. Another paper supports the broader pathway by saying microplastics can persist in the environment and act as a route for harmful contaminants in the food chain, with hazardous chemicals such as persistent organic pollutants depositing on microplastic surfaces [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. Similarly, a review on seafood and public health states that microplastics can disrupt the food chain and create public health challenges for humans who consume seafood, while noting widespread environmental release and ecological exposure [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000]. A Bangladesh study strengthens the concern by reporting that all commercial fish feeds it examined were contaminated with microplastics, with mean abundances of 500–2200 MPs/kg, and by framing this as a concern for sustainable aquaculture because people in developing countries depend heavily on farmed fish for protein [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: In men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, elevated FSH is associated with a more clearly abnormal clinical and hormonal profile, especially in the Klinefelter syndrome (KS) group, which also showed lower testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher LH, greater height and arm span, and more gynecomastia than the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. The study also found that men with testicular XX DSD had LH, FSH, and penile length values that were intermediate between KS and the undefined-cause group, suggesting a phenotype that is less severe than KS but not fully normal [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper concluded that clinical and laboratory data can differentiate men with chromosomal anomalies, particularly KS and testicular XX, from those with undefined causes [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. In contrast, another NOA cohort study linked elevated serum FSH and LH to failed sperm retrieval, while successful retrieval was associated with larger testicular volumes and a higher T/LH ratio, and multivariate analysis identified serum FSH, bilateral testicular volumes, and T/LH ratio as significant predictors of successful sperm extraction [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the provided evidence from that study does not report subgroup comparisons for chromosomal anomalies, KS, or testicular XX DSD, so it cannot directly address how those groups compare with an undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from the Y-chromosome anomaly study adds that several karyotype categories beyond 46,XY/45,X should be referred for AZF deletion screening, but its only explicit laboratory association was that higher sperm counts were rarely linked to Y-chromosome microdeletions [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the strongest direct evidence for your question comes from the KS/testicular XX DSD study, which shows that elevated FSH is part of a broader pattern of testicular and androgen abnormalities in KS and is intermediate in testicular XX DSD relative to undefined causes [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The supplied papers support a link between NEDD4 and growth-factor signaling, but only one paper directly connects its functional effects to IGF1/IGF1R dependence. In gastric cancer cell lines, NEDD4 knockdown or overexpression altered tumor growth only in IGF1R-dependent cells and not in IGF1R-independent cells, indicating that NEDD4’s impact is context-specific and tied to dependence on the IGF1/IGF1R pathway [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000]. That same study reports that a PTEN-IRS1 axis is required for NEDD4-mediated regulation of Akt activation and tumor growth, and that NEDD4 promotes proliferation of IGF1/IGF1R-dependent gastric cancer cells by antagonizing PTEN’s protein phosphatase activity toward IRS1 [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. The clinical context also aligns with this pathway dependence, because NEDD4 is higher in IGF1-high gastric cancer tissues than in IGF1-low tissues and normal tissues, and co-high expression of NEDD4 and IGF1 predicts worse prognosis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Separate evidence from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma shows that NEDD4 is translationally upregulated, with polysomal profiling suggesting its higher protein expression arises from translational activation [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. However, that pancreatic study links NEDD4 to PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling rather than to IGF1 specifically, so it supports a broader growth-signaling role but not a direct IGF1 pathway mechanism [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the provided summaries, the main agreement is that NEDD4 promotes tumor-associated signaling and proliferation in a pathway-dependent manner, while the main limitation is that direct evidence for translational regulation of NEDD4 within the IGF1 pathway is only indirectly supported by the gastric cancer study and not established by the other papers [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: Across the papers, textile waste management is most consistently framed as a shift from disposal toward recovery, recycling, and value-added conversion within a circular economy [https://openalex.org/W3205047951||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies emphasize converting textile waste into new products or secondary raw materials, including recycled fibers, biobased composites, nonwovens, and construction or geotechnical materials [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4411396683||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4205579211||ABSTRACT||000]. For cotton waste specifically, surface modification can increase adsorption of dyes and heavy metals, and cotton waste fibers can show high adsorption capacity for removing recalcitrant pollutants from wastewater [https://openalex.org/W3137350553||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, adsorption is presented as a practical tertiary wastewater-treatment step for textile effluents because it can remove dyes and metals, especially when combined with primary and secondary treatment [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. In contrast, other papers do not provide adsorption-based applications and instead focus on biological treatment, enzymatic recycling, pyrolysis, or mechanical/chemical recycling as waste-conversion routes [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4411396683||ABSTRACT||000]. The evidence also suggests that textile waste is challenging to recycle because of mixed fibers, finishes, and additives, so pretreatment and material characterization are often needed before conversion can be efficient and economically viable [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4205579211||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the strongest synthesis is that waste conversion can create useful secondary materials, while adsorption is especially useful when textile waste or wastewater is being converted into sorbents for contaminant removal [https://openalex.org/W3137350553||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How sustainability reporting link with SDGs and sustainability performance, it matter from the supply chain framework too?
final_answer: Across the papers, sustainability reporting is presented as a way to assess and communicate sustainability performance, while also improving transparency, accountability, and alignment with broader standards such as GRI and other reporting frameworks [https://openalex.org/W4402984150||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies connect reporting to the SDGs more directly: one paper argues that corporate sustainability reporting following GRI guidelines helps show whether and how SDGs matter to the private sector, and another shows that SDG-linked reporting can be turned into a reporting score index that helps stakeholders measure firms’ sustainable performance and commitment to the global agenda [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392003298||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence also suggests that reporting and SDG disclosure can be weakly connected to actual performance, because firms may cite SDGs without explaining how initiatives change business contribution, and another large-sample study found a disconnect between corporate sustainability performance and SDG reporting [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4394576889||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, other papers report a positive relationship between sustainable supply chains and SDGs, and between sustainable supply chains and financial performance, implying that supply chain practice can be a concrete pathway through which SDG-related sustainability performance is realized [https://openalex.org/W4394886303||ABSTRACT||001]. Supply chain evidence is especially strong where environmental sustainability is influenced by customer relationships, postponement, information sharing, and information quality, and where environmental sustainability in turn mediates links between most supply chain practices and financial performance [https://openalex.org/W3132273715||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate framework paper also proposes sustainability assessment for global supply chains using 91 indicators and says this helps measure both a company’s own and its suppliers’ sustainability performance and communicate progress to stakeholders [https://openalex.org/W4400657024||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study explicitly proposes a framework for achieving SDGs through sustainable supply chain management and states that sustainability reporting/measurement should be tracked through supply-chain-based indicators [https://openalex.org/W4327714039||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the literature suggests that sustainability reporting matters for SDGs most when it is tied to measurable supply chain performance rather than treated as symbolic disclosure, but several studies also indicate that current reporting often falls short of demonstrating real performance improvements [https://openalex.org/W4220859323||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4394576889||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In the manufacturing firms study, how did SS relate to sustainability audits, and how is that different from the Metaverse study where SS had no significant impact on student perceptions?
final_answer: In the manufacturing-firms study, SS was reported as having a significant positive relationship with sustainability audits, meaning it was associated with higher sustainability audit activity rather than no effect [https://openalex.org/W4327860571||ABSTRACT||000]. A related manufacturing-firms summary also states that sustainability assurance (SS) had a positive and significant effect on auditing practices, including sustainability audits, while audit failures were insignificant [https://openalex.org/W4388577720||ABSTRACT||000]. Another manufacturing-firms abstract adds that audit committee characteristics were linked to better sustainability assurance quality, although sustainability assurance rates were still significantly low and quality was poor [https://openalex.org/W3140995767||ABSTRACT||000]. By contrast, the Metaverse study evidence available here does not report a significant SS effect on student perceptions; instead, it shows that perceptions toward social sustainability were significantly influenced by performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, and extraversion, while effort expectancy and social influence had no significant impact on SS [https://openalex.org/W4391131066||ABSTRACT||001]. So, across the provided evidence, SS is tied to stronger audit-related outcomes in manufacturing firms, whereas the Metaverse evidence centers on other predictors of student perceptions and does not show a significant SS effect [https://openalex.org/W4327860571||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4391131066||ABSTRACT||001]. The main limitation is that the summaries do not provide a direct Metaverse result stating “SS had no significant impact on student perceptions,” so the comparison rests on the absence of such a finding in the supplied Metaverse evidence rather than a directly quoted contradiction [https://openalex.org/W4391131066||ABSTRACT||001].

query: In the sustainability assessment of district heating systems, which multi-criteria decision analysis methods were compared, and what did the sensitivity analysis reveal about their suitability and differences in calculation and interpretation?
final_answer: The district-heating-specific study compared five MCDA methods: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA, using 8 criteria for 12 district heating companies [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Its sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in three ways: one-by-one to identify stability ranges for alternatives, one-by-one with a fixed value to examine effects on average scores, and by contrasting AHP weighting with equal weighting [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The analysis, together with the literature review, concluded that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analyses of district heating systems [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the study emphasized that the methods differ in calculation process and in how their results are interpreted [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers in the supplied set do compare MCDA methods for sustainability problems, such as DEMATEL, REMBRANDT, and VIKOR in one study and TOPSIS, VIKOR, COMET, and PROMETHEE II in another, but these do not provide district-heating-specific sensitivity results [https://openalex.org/W3196060399||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3202401363||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports the view that multiple MCDA methods can be appropriate for sustainability assessment, but the district-heating paper is the only one in the supplied set that directly identifies both the compared methods and the sensitivity-analysis findings requested [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do the sustainability ideas in the supply chain management framework and the article on sustainable marketing both show how environmental sustainability can be advanced and linked to company image?
final_answer: Across the supply chain management papers, environmental sustainability is advanced by embedding sustainability into core business systems rather than treating it as a separate add-on. One framework organizes 789 sustainable business practices into 11 categories under a triple-bottom-line logic, while another argues that companies need a sustainability mindset, a systems perspective, and stakeholder coordination to address broader challenges such as climate change and the Sustainable Development Goals [https://openalex.org/W4283697438||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308101885||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies also show that sustainability becomes operational through concrete management practices, including customer relationships, postponement, information sharing, information quality, organizational learning, and collaboration across the supply chain [https://openalex.org/W3132273715||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3183301120||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, these supply chain frameworks connect sustainability to company image indirectly by tying it to profit, performance, leadership, and a firm’s broader identity as a sustainable business [https://openalex.org/W4283697438||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3183301120||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3128290205||ABSTRACT||000]. The sustainable marketing article makes this link more explicit by stating that sustainability is part of a company’s image and brand identity, building reputation, customer trust, loyalty, and competitive advantage [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001]. It also says sustainable marketing strategies help improve image and reputation while attracting new customers and differentiating the business from competitors [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the papers agree that environmental sustainability can strengthen company image when it is integrated into strategy, operations, and market-facing behavior, though the supply chain papers emphasize internal systems and the marketing paper emphasizes external brand effects [https://openalex.org/W3135028795||ABSTRACT||002] [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001]. A limitation is that the evidence set contains stronger direct support for company image from the sustainable marketing article than from the supply chain articles, so the comparison is partly indirect [https://openalex.org/W4383567484||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4283697438||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do sustainable technologies, such as clean energy in manufacturing and green and reverse logistics, support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises, and what did the analysis find about enterprise adoption and environmental management?
final_answer: Across the papers, sustainable technologies are consistently presented as enabling Industry 4.0-driven innovation and SDG-oriented growth by improving environmental sustainability, production efficiency, and organizational capabilities. Industry 4.0 is described as strengthening capabilities such as green absorptive capacity, sustainable partnership, and sustainable innovation orientation, which in turn support green process innovation and the development or reintroduction of eco-friendly products in an economical and competitive way [https://openalex.org/W3189862204||ABSTRACT||001]. A broader review likewise finds that Industry 4.0 technologies can improve environmental sustainability across production, supply chains, delivery chains, and market outcomes, and concludes that these technologies appear environmentally sustainable because they help manufacture goods more efficiently while reducing resource consumption [https://openalex.org/W4226256571||ABSTRACT||001]. More specifically, one study links sustainable technologies such as clean energy in manufacturing and green/reverse logistics with Industry 4.0 innovations and SDGs, finding significant relationships between green manufacturing, green logistics, reverse logistics, and technologies including autonomous robots, renewable energy, advanced materials, virtual technologies, and simulation [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||001]. That study also reports that more than 82% of the surveyed enterprises implement the SDGs and more than 70% prefer environmental aspects in business management, suggesting substantial enterprise uptake of sustainability-oriented practices in its Slovak sample [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. In line with this, the analysis found significant links between environmental management under the SDGs and sustainability in production and logistics, including renewable energy use, waste separation and recycling, environmental certification, environmental training, and continuous CO2 reduction in logistics activities [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the literature is not uniformly optimistic: one review notes that Industry 4.0 and related technologies can also create negative environmental effects such as air pollution, improper waste disposal, and excessive use of raw materials, information, and energy, and it identifies a gap between current and intended sustainable production conditions [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||000]. Other reviews reinforce the SDG connection by showing that Industry 4.0 supports circular economy practices and links them to SDGs such as clean energy, responsible consumption and production, and climate action, while also proposing frameworks for organizational realignment rather than reporting direct adoption outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4210290448||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that sustainable technologies support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth through cleaner, more efficient, and more circular production and logistics systems, but adoption appears uneven and several studies emphasize barriers, early-stage development, or the need for further research and implementation guidance [https://openalex.org/W4288738282||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3173460341||ABSTRACT||001].

query: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
final_answer: The systematic review says that OSC has been proven to enhance environmental performance by reducing waste generation and carbon emissions [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. It also reports that, by 2018, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration, despite these documented benefits [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. This contrast between clear environmental gains and limited market uptake is part of why the review argues it is timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The review further frames this as useful for learning strategies, especially by comparing developed and developing regions to understand what supports better performance [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate review on sustainability impacts similarly emphasizes that environmental outcomes are highly context dependent and that there are still significant evidence gaps, which supports the need to identify the drivers behind improved performance [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence base presented here consistently points to positive environmental potential for OSC but limited diffusion and a need for comparative, context-sensitive analysis [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3129330537||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does the study use predictive analytics in the 1-hop work, and what does the 2-hop AI impact assessment say about AI"s role for sustainable development?
final_answer: Across the provided papers, the 1-hop work is not described with enough detail to identify a specific predictive-analytics method; several summaries explicitly say the evidence does not specify how predictive analytics is used, and instead only indicate broader sustainability or SDG-oriented AI applications [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3135629427||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400511829||ABSTRACT||001]. Where the 1-hop framing is described, it generally treats AI as supporting sustainability goals and SDGs while also recognizing that AI itself must be developed responsibly [https://openalex.org/W3135539146||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4395007039||ABSTRACT||001]. The 2-hop AI impact assessments consistently say AI should not be assumed to be inherently sustainable, because its role includes both enabling and inhibiting effects that depend on how it is developed and governed [https://openalex.org/W4319018126||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3135629427||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies stress that AI can support sustainable development through climate action, resource management, healthcare, transport, agriculture, energy, and other sectors, but only if ecological, algorithmic, social, and economic risks are actively managed [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392387614||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the papers warn that AI brings harms such as energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, bias, discrimination, inequality, and nontransparent decision-making [https://openalex.org/W4392387614||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390684506||ABSTRACT||000]. The most explicit assessment framework says only a comprehensive evaluation of both AI’s ends and means can justify a claim of “thick” sustainability, whereas selective assessment supports at most “thin” sustainability [https://openalex.org/W4319018126||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, the literature agrees that sustainable development analysis should be multidimensional, aligned with the SDGs, and attentive to stakeholders, infrastructure constraints, and governance across the AI lifecycle [https://openalex.org/W4392387614||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3126217793||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3135539146||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?
final_answer: Across these papers, environmental sustainability is consistently treated as something that must be achieved through practical construction decisions rather than as a purely conceptual goal [https://openalex.org/W4386122897||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4221129459||ABSTRACT||000]. In off-site construction research, sustainability is presented as a multi-theme area spanning environmental, economic, social, decision-making, optimization, and industry-management topics, and the literature review maps gaps and future directions using 272 studies [https://openalex.org/W4297722265||ABSTRACT||000]. That off-site literature also highlights concrete environmental gains such as reduced waste generation, lower carbon emissions, improved efficiency, and lower time and cost, while noting that OSC adoption remained limited and below 20% in major markets by 2018 [https://openalex.org/W4321507223||ABSTRACT||000]. The Ghana barrier studies connect sustainability implementation barriers to residential buildings by showing that barriers such as management, standards, society, and knowledge constraints can obstruct sustainable construction at every stage, with management-related barriers described as the most significant [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001]. They also report that green building principles could improve environmental ecosystem and social cohesion, but only if substantial investment is made and the barriers are addressed first [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001]. In a related Ghana residential-building study, environmental sustainability is tied to life-cycle indicators including water quality, air quality, energy use and conservation, and environmental compliance and management [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||001]. The Saudi Arabia “Mostadam” approach is not described in the provided evidence, so only the broader connection can be stated: both the Ghana barrier work and the off-site construction literature show that sustainability advances depend on implementation capacity, not just technical goals [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4297722265||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the shared sustainability-related finding across the contexts is that green or sustainable construction is linked to better environmental performance, but progress is slowed by awareness, knowledge, management, regulatory, and cost-related barriers [https://openalex.org/W4386122897||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4221129459||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4212912827||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What did the interviews with retailers and service providers in North America reveal about managing product returns sustainably?
final_answer: The interviews with multichannel retailers, retail experts, and return service providers in the UK and North America found that retailers were paying attention to the financial impact of returns, but they had little awareness of the environmental scale of returns and no comprehensive approach to managing that impact sustainably [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The evidence suggests a gap between recognizing returns as a business cost and treating them as a sustainability issue, because retailers focused on financial consequences rather than environmental ones [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study indicates that sustainable practice can be undermined by paradoxes, implying that return management should avoid actions that create conflicting outcomes [https://openalex.org/W3135380255||ABSTRACT||001]. Consistent with that, the same paper urges retailers to move toward cradle-to-cradle, closed-loop lifecycle supply chains and to evaluate whether adopted practices actually support sustainability goals [https://openalex.org/W3135380255||ABSTRACT||001]. It also emphasizes considering the whole supply chain and the role of each actor when implementing sustainable practices, which aligns with the need for coordinated returns management across retailers and service providers [https://openalex.org/W3135380255||ABSTRACT||001]. The paper on returns management further concludes that retailers face barriers to developing environmental sustainability plans and proposes strategies and a framework to reduce the environmental impact of product returns [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the interviews reveal an emerging awareness of returns as a sustainability problem, but one that is still underdeveloped in practice and in need of clearer frameworks, supply-chain coordination, and more holistic planning [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3135380255||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The clearest description of the selection process comes from the study that searched Scopus for the keywords “Sustainability assessment” OR “Life cycle assessment” AND “Internal combustion engine*” OR “ICE*,” and then “carefully screening” the results to obtain 87 life cycle assessment studies published between 2017 and 2023 [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. Another review indicates that a PRISMA protocol and literature searches in scientific databases were used, followed by an evaluation matrix to synthesize evidence, but it does not list the specific inclusion or exclusion criteria for the 87 studies [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the available summaries, the 87 studies were categorized using multiple analytical dimensions rather than a single rule: one paper grouped them by six aspects—sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies (including alternative fuels), types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate review classified case studies through an evaluation matrix with integrated criteria, and its explicit category counts show 52 of 84 case studies using stand-alone LCA, 8 using LCC combined with other analyses, and none using S-LCA [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. The evidence also suggests that some reviews limited their scope to peer-reviewed journal articles over defined time spans, such as 1960 to 2022, but those criteria were reported for a broader sustainability-assessment review rather than for the 87-study set itself [https://openalex.org/W4403910234||ABSTRACT||000]. In addition, one summary notes an S-LCA emphasis on production stage and system boundaries such as cradle-to-use and cradle-to-grave, but it does not connect those rules to the 87-study selection process [https://openalex.org/W3186802024||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the available evidence shows keyword-based database searching, PRISMA-style screening, and multi-criterion classification, but it does not provide a complete, explicit set of inclusion/exclusion rules for how the 87 studies were selected [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What thematic analysis procedure and inter-coder reliability metrics were used to analyze the interviews, focus groups, and observations?
final_answer: Across the papers that actually analyzed interviews, focus groups, and/or observations, thematic analysis was the common approach, but the level of procedural detail varied substantially. One study used intra- and inter-case analysis during data collection, combining thematic analysis with analytical questioning and systemic modeling, and it was strengthened by critical reflexive dialogue among the research team, collaborators, and an expert panel [pmc_PMC10136404||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study simply states that semistructured interviews and focus group discussions were coded using thematic analysis, but it does not specify the steps of the procedure beyond that description [pmc_PMC9890762||ABSTRACT||000]. A third paper gives the most explicit workflow: it used deductive thematic analysis in which codes were grouped into sub-themes across questions and then abstracted into themes related to uncertainty management, yielding 727 codes, 92 sub-themes, 18 themes, and one meta-theme [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||002]. A fourth paper reports a deductive/inductive thematic analysis to identify patterns in how leading IR reporters disclosed SDG contributions and legitimacy, but it does not provide a detailed analytic workflow for interviews, focus groups, or observations [https://openalex.org/W4281686775||ABSTRACT||001]. None of these qualitative summaries reports specific inter-coder reliability metrics such as kappa or percent agreement; instead, they either explicitly note that no such metrics were reported or provide only general collaborative/ reflexive procedures [pmc_PMC10136404||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9890762||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||002] [https://openalex.org/W4281686775||ABSTRACT||001]. One additional paper in the set is not directly relevant to thematic analysis because it concerns AIS scoring reliability, using ICC rather than qualitative coding metrics [pmc_PMC10229665||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests thematic analysis was typically used with either deductive or mixed deductive/inductive coding, but the reporting of inter-coder reliability was minimal to absent [pmc_PMC10136404||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9890762||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||002].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: In hepatocellular carcinoma, macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was reported to be significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line, and its expression was positively correlated with cyclin D1 and tumor size [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. Knockdown of MIF by siRNA inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in an in vivo xenograft model, while not affecting the cell cycle [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. Mechanistically, MIF knockdown was associated with downregulation of cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, along with upregulation of Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence suggests that MIF supports HCC cell growth and survival, and that reducing MIF reverses these pro-tumor signals [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. The other supplied papers do not provide additional primary evidence about MIF in HCC or MIF knockdown effects, so the conclusion rests on a single study [pmc_PMC3162940||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9890137||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10140795||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the supplied studies, coronary artery calcification is consistently associated with worse outcomes, but the type of complication differs by population and setting. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, higher coronary artery calcium score was associated with all-cause mortality over 4.4 years, with only modest discrimination for prognosis [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In level-1 trauma patients, left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with any complication (OR 3.9, 95% CI 1.7–8.9) and with adverse discharge condition, and a greater number of calcified coronary arteries showed a trend toward more complications [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. In heavily calcified coronary lesions treated with orbital atherectomy, the calcification burden was substantial and was associated with the need for invasive imaging and plaque modification, including superficial sanding in 90% of vessels and fracturing of deeper medial calcium in 63% of vessels [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||000]. Despite that procedural complexity, the atherectomy series reported 66% device success, 94% procedural success, and no primary safety events during 30 days of follow-up [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. Broader cardiovascular literature in the summaries also indicates that CAC predicts future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and improves risk prediction when added to the Framingham risk score [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the summaries also show important limits: no clinical trial has shown that CAC screening improves clinical outcomes or healthcare costs, and similar CAC levels may correspond to different absolute risks across regions and ethnic groups [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports CAC as a marker of higher risk for mortality, in-hospital complications, and greater procedural complexity, but not as a proven intervention target that itself has established outcome benefit [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF appears to improve HCC diagnosis by leveraging two markers with opposite expression patterns in patients with HCC: serum KAI1 is downregulated, while VEGF is upregulated [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. In the same study, KAI1 was associated with TNM staging, intrahepatic metastasis, lymph node/peritoneal metastasis, and portal vein thrombus, while VEGF was closely related to alpha-fetoprotein level, suggesting that the two markers may capture different clinically relevant aspects of disease [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. Diagnostic performance was better when both markers were used together than when either was used alone, with sensitivity increasing from 86.96% to 91.86%, accuracy from 83.06% to 84.68%, and negative predictive value to 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The reported AUCs also indicate that KAI1 alone performed better than VEGF alone in this dataset, with AUCs of 0.907 and 0.779, respectively, which supports the idea that combining markers can add value beyond VEGF alone [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The authors conclude that combined KAI1 and VEGF detection may greatly improve diagnostic efficiency and provide a reliable diagnostic marker panel for HCC [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the other supplied summaries do not provide additional biomarker evidence for KAI1 and VEGF, so the broader generalizability of this conclusion cannot be assessed from the available text [pmc_PMC9806080||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8318739||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3178660840||ABSTRACT||001].

final_answer: The provided evidence indicates that the DIEP reconstruction learning curve improved over time, but mainly through better efficiency rather than broad changes in outcomes. query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal mouse cardiac injury models are described as crucial tools for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of cardiac regeneration because newborn mice retain a short period of full regenerative capacity after injury, and this neonatal feature may also apply to the human neonatal heart [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. These models are said to help identify factors that can stimulate adult heart repair by inducing endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which in turn informs novel therapeutic strategies for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. The same summary notes that findings from established injury models, together with studies in large animals and humans, can provide additional insight that may pave the way for regenerative medicine approaches [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. In the provided evidence, no other paper directly addresses neonatal injury models; several summaries explicitly state that their topics are unrelated to regeneration, such as LVAD-mediated myocardial recovery, heart valve implants, neonatal monitoring algorithms, or infant care interventions [pmc_PMC9806425||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10143004||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10230358||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9762362||ABSTRACT||000]. One mechanistically related but non-neonatal study reported that chronic ISO/PE treatment in mice produced growth, collagen deposition, and transcriptional changes that more closely recapitulated early pressure overload-induced heart failure and human hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but it did not mention regeneration [pmc_PMC8921177||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports the idea that neonatal injury models are used as a developmental window to discover regeneration-associated mechanisms that may be leveraged in adult hearts, while also showing that the rest of the provided papers do not directly test or extend that claim [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The ClinicalTrials.gov-related evidence for the DECISION study is inconsistent across the provided summaries, with different papers reporting different trial registration identifiers and different descriptions of the study. One paper describes DECISION as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial in patients with locally advanced/metastatic RAI-refractory DTC, designed to test whether sorafenib improves progression-free survival [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraq study from Nineveh governorate, researchers compared maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination in 1-day-old imported Cobb 500 and Ross 308 broiler chicks using 707 blood samples from 28 Ross 308 flocks and 17 Cobb 500 flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Both broiler types showed high and uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 chicks performed better overall than Ross 308 chicks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Specifically, Cobb 500 had a higher antibody-positive rate than Ross 308 (100% vs 97.78%), a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), and a lower mean CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%), indicating better uniformity [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The study also reported a higher mean vaccination index for Cobb 500 than Ross 308 (966.59 vs 821.60) [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. Based on these findings, Cobb 500 was the better-performing strain in this study [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. The other provided papers do not address this Iraq broiler comparison directly, so they do not add evidence about the specific strains or maternal antibody outcome in question [pmc_PMC4172590||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10330971||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, mask mandates are generally associated with fewer COVID-19 infections, especially when they are sustained and well complied with [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. In a US state-level analysis, mask mandates were estimated to offset about one third of the case-growth increase associated with higher mobility, and states with higher compliance saw greater benefit [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. That study also estimated that a national mask mandate beginning on May 15, 2020 would have reduced total US infections on November 15, 2020 by 23.7% to 30.4% [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate study found that keeping face mask mandates in place for at least two months, rather than less than one month, was associated with lower COVID-19 incidence, with reductions ranging from 4 fewer cases per 100,000 in low-social-vulnerability counties to 401 fewer cases per 100,000 in high-social-vulnerability counties [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from healthcare-worker PPE reviews is consistent with this direction of effect, showing that face masks significantly protect against infection, with especially strong support for N95 masks, while surgical masks performed better than cloth masks [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. However, one ventilation-focused study cautioned that masks can be counterproductive if used inappropriately with ventilation, suggesting that mask policies work best when combined with proper environmental controls [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence in these summaries supports mask mandates as a useful non-pharmaceutical intervention for reducing COVID-19 spread, but the magnitude of benefit appears to depend on compliance, duration, and context [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: Across the machining-focused papers, nano-enhancers are presented as better for mitigating workpiece burn mainly because they improve cooling, lubrication, and heat transfer during cutting or grinding [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. In titanium alloy grinding, nano-enhancers are recommended because their high thermal conductivity helps solve burn problems by improving lubrication and cooling compared with traditional cutting fluids, and high-hardness spherical particles are described as especially suitable [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. For MQL machining, nano-enhanced biolubricants are said to improve tool wear and surface integrity through advanced lubrication and heat-transfer mechanisms, along with distinctive film formation, atomization, and infiltration behaviors [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. The evidence also suggests that nano-enhancers can help dry machining by enabling tools with finer microstructures, higher density, higher hardness, greater wear resistance, and better thermal stability, and by improving fracture toughness and thermal shock resistance when SiC whiskers are added to alumina-based ceramic tools [https://openalex.org/W4391982892||ABSTRACT||001]. These material and tribological benefits are consistent with the broader goal of reducing surface burn, including burn in nickel-based alloy grinding, but the exact action of nano-enhanced biolubricants is still described as indistinct and dependent on many factors such as enhancer type, lubricant type, concentration, droplet size, and dispersion [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. Several other summaries do not provide direct evidence about workpiece burn or nano-enhancers in machining, and one paper is explicitly about skin-burn treatment rather than machining, so they cannot substantiate the claim directly [https://openalex.org/W4375866196||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4322505914||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3196394368||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4207036872||ABSTRACT||001][https://openalex.org/W4324057306||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) played the role of a solid nano-additive in a specific canola-oil lubrication study, where it was used to improve canola oil’s tribological performance because canola oil alone was described as insufficient compared with petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The study tested canola oil with 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% hBN nanoparticles, and also examined combinations with graphene nanoplatelets [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. Its evaluation included dynamic viscosity measurements and pin-on-disk tests in the boundary lubrication regime, with coefficient of friction and wear analyses reported [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. For hBN alone, 1.0 wt.% gave the lowest coefficient of friction, which was reported as 40% lower than the base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. When hBN was combined with graphene nanoplatelets, the formulation showed a synergistic effect, reducing friction by 56% and wear by 90% versus base oil, attributed to a composite protective film and polishing mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. Across the other supplied papers, hBN is discussed only more generally as a tribologically functional nanoparticle in biolubricant reviews, while canola oil is mentioned as a bio-lubricant base oil or plant-based lubricant source without hBN-specific testing details [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4401870224||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000]. These review papers also emphasize that bio-lubricants are assessed for viscosity index, lubricity, biodegradability, renewability, and low toxicity, but they note drawbacks such as lower thermo-oxidative stability and higher pour points [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence indicates that hBN’s role was as an additive intended to enhance canola oil’s lubrication performance, and the study evaluated it through viscosity, friction, and wear testing rather than through broader sustainability metrics [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
final_answer: The clearest Romania-specific evidence shows that a subnational SDG Index was built using an indicator-based, integrated approach with 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database to measure progress toward the SDGs at local and regional level [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. This approach was used to compare territorial performance across Romania rather than only at the national level, and the results showed that the highest sustainable development performance is concentrated in specific geographical areas [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. In contrast, the poorest performers were identified as rural areas and extended peripheral regions in the eastern and southern parts of Romania [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. Broader European papers in the set reinforce the idea that regional SDG monitoring depends on robust indicator frameworks, regional benchmarking, and adaptable data infrastructure, but they do not provide Romania-specific results [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: The strongest direct evidence suggests that organizational learning capability can contribute to radical innovation by serving as a mediating mechanism that translates leadership behavior into innovation outcomes. In one study, organizational learning capability fully mediated the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, indicating that learning capability is the pathway through which leadership influences radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. That paper also describes organizational learning capability as creating a context that promotes experimentation, dialog, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment, all of which are argued to support radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. Related evidence from other papers is consistent with the broader idea that learning-oriented capabilities support deeper change, but these studies focus on sustainability, transformation, or innovation capability rather than radical innovation specifically [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000]. For example, organizational learning is reported as important for sustainable organizational performance and innovation that is well-informed and well-processed, while networking and innovation intervene in its relationship with performance [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study finds that ambidextrous learning is positively associated with adopting sustainable business model innovations, suggesting that learning can support novel strategic change even if radical innovation is not directly tested [https://openalex.org/W4323928282||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence implies that organizational learning capability contributes to radical innovation by enabling experimentation, openness to external input, and internal conditions for change, but the broader literature provided mostly addresses adjacent outcomes rather than radical innovation itself [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4320476375||ABSTRACT||000].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
final_answer: In hepatocellular carcinoma, one study found that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line, and its expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and tumor size [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. siRNA-mediated MIF knockdown inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, did not alter the cell cycle, and reduced tumor growth in an in vivo xenograft model [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. At the protein level, MIF knockdown increased Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, while decreasing cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK in HCC cells [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the other provided summaries, no additional HCC-specific evidence on MIF or its knockdown was reported, so the available synthesis rests on this single HCC study [pmc_PMC10140795||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC3162940||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC9890137||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports a pro-tumor role for MIF in HCC, with knockdown shifting cells toward reduced growth and increased apoptosis alongside suppression of Akt/ERK- and cyclin D1-associated signaling [pmc_PMC4170598||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, coronary artery calcification (CAC) is most consistently associated with worse prognostic outcomes and complications, but the strength and meaning of that association vary by setting [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In symptomatic patients referred for cardiac CT, higher coronary artery calcium score predicted mortality over a median follow-up of 4.4 years, and coronary calcification measures were used as prognostic markers in both women and men [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In level-1 trauma patients, left main coronary artery calcification was independently associated with any complication, and coronary artery calcification on routine CT was concluded to be associated with in-hospital complications overall [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. That trauma study also found a trend for increasing numbers of calcified coronary arteries to be associated with complications, with a significant association with adverse discharge condition, while pulmonary emphysema and aortic calcifications were not associated with complications [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. A broader review similarly states that CAC is associated with future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and improves risk prediction when added to the Framingham risk score [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the same review notes that the clinical meaning of a given CAC level is not uniform across regions and ethnic groups, and that no clinical trial has yet shown that CAC screening improves outcomes or healthcare costs [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. Some provided papers do not directly address CAC-related complications at all, so the evidence base here is limited to indirect prognostic data and one trauma cohort rather than a broad complication-specific literature [pmc_PMC10140970||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8758654||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9806495||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10141707||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF appears to improve HCC diagnosis by leveraging two markers with opposite expression patterns in HCC, since KAI1 is downregulated while VEGF is upregulated in HCC tissues and serum [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. In the cited study, serum KAI1 was associated with TNM stage, metastasis, and portal vein thrombus, while VEGF was also closely related to α-fetoprotein level, suggesting that the two markers may capture complementary aspects of tumor behavior [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. As individual diagnostic markers, KAI1 had an AUC of 0.907 and VEGF had an AUC of 0.779 for diagnosing HCC, indicating that KAI1 was the stronger single marker in this dataset [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. When combined, KAI1 and VEGF increased sensitivity to 91.86%, accuracy to 84.68%, and negative predictive value to 78.79% compared with KAI1 alone, and the authors concluded that this greatly improved diagnostic efficiency [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. The available evidence therefore supports a modest diagnostic gain from combining the two markers rather than relying on either one alone [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence provided does not include details on sample size, study design, or external validation, so the robustness and generalizability of the improvement cannot be assessed from these summaries alone [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. Other provided papers do not address KAI1/VEGF or HCC diagnosis and therefore do not add supporting evidence for this question [pmc_PMC9806080||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8318739||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3178660840||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
final_answer: Based on the supplied evidence, the only paper that actually reports a learning-curve change over time is the institutional DIEP reconstruction study, which found gradual improvement across the study period rather than a sharp step change [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. At the institutional level, the clearest improvement was a shorter length of hospital stay in the late group compared with the early group, while most other outcomes did not differ significantly between the start and end of the study [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. For the single surgeon, the learning curve was more evident in operative efficiency, with a significant reduction in total surgery time over time as experience accumulated [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. This suggests that the learning curve became easier to see in process measures like hospital stay and total surgery time than in postoperative complications [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. The other provided papers do not contribute DIEP-specific learning-curve data: one is a review of machine learning applications in breast surgery, one compares reconstruction types and notes increasing secondary reconstruction after implant-only reconstruction, and one reviews uptake of immediate breast reconstruction in older women [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10364779||ABSTRACT||000]. So, from the evidence provided, the answer is that the DIEP learning curve improved over time, mainly through shorter hospital stay and reduced operative time, but the magnitude and consistency of improvement were limited for other outcomes [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models help explain adult heart cardiac regeneration by revealing that the newborn heart has a transient regenerative capacity that is lost later, making neonatal injury a useful window into pro-regenerative biology [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. In neonatal mouse injury models, cardiac injury can induce endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation, which the paper describes as a mechanism that may point toward therapies for diseased adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. The same summary also states that these models are crucial for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying cardiac regenerative processes and may even be relevant to the neonatal human heart [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraqi broiler chick study, the researchers compared maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination in 1-day-old imported chicks from Ross 308 and Cobb 500 flocks in Mosul governorate, using 707 blood samples from 28 Ross 308 flocks and 17 Cobb 500 flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Cobb 500 chicks performed better overall than Ross 308 chicks because all Cobb 500 chicks were antibody-positive, compared with 97.78% of Ross 308 chicks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Cobb 500 also had a higher mean maternal antibody titer than Ross 308 (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76) and a lower mean CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%), indicating more uniform titers [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The study concluded that both strains had high and uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 produced higher protective titers than Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. No other provided paper summary contained relevant evidence to challenge or refine this comparison, so the available evidence consistently favors Cobb 500 in this study [pmc_PMC10330971||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8703754||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000].
