query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the included studies, mask mandates and mask use were generally associated with fewer COVID-19 cases or lower infection risk, although the strength of evidence varies by setting and study design. In US state-level data, mask mandates were estimated to offset about one third of the cases-growth increase associated with higher mobility, and a hypothetical national mandate starting May 15, 2020 was projected to reduce total US infections by 23.7% to 30.4% by November 15, 2020, with greater effectiveness in states with higher compliance [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. A county-level study likewise found that keeping prevention policies in place for longer durations was associated with lower COVID-19 incidence, and for face mask mandates the monthly incidence difference ranged from -4 per 100,000 in low social vulnerability counties to -401 per 100,000 in high social vulnerability counties [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. At the individual-protection level, a rapid review and meta-analysis found that wearing PPE, including face masks, significantly protected healthcare workers from infection, and another study reported that surgical masks provided better protection than cloth masks [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence also suggests that masks are not uniformly beneficial in every context: one paper warned that masks can be counterproductive if inappropriately used with ventilation, while the best approach was combining a face mask with upward ventilation, which reduced indoor infectious concentration by nearly 99.95% compared with no precautions [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the studies agree that masks or mask mandates can reduce transmission, but their impact depends on compliance, duration, population vulnerability, and correct use alongside other measures [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001].

query: Why nano-enhancers better for workpiece burn?
final_answer: The strongest evidence for why nano-enhancers may be better for reducing workpiece burn comes from the machining-focused papers, which describe nano-enhanced biolubricants as improving lubrication and heat transfer compared with biolubricant-based MQL machining, thereby helping reduce machining problems such as workpiece burn [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. In titanium alloy grinding specifically, nano-enhancers are recommended because their high thermal conductivity improves lubrication and cooling performance, which is proposed to solve the workpiece burn problem [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also says nano-enhancers with high hardness and spherical characteristics are better choices, suggesting they may help address wheel wear and nickel-based alloy surface burn [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001]. More broadly, the literature notes that nano-enhanced biolubricants are associated with better tool wear and surface integrity in experimental studies, although their exact actions during preparation, atomization, infiltration, heat transfer, and anti-friction remain indistinct [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000]. Several other papers only support the idea indirectly by stating that nanomaterials can improve properties, process precision, or sustainable manufacturing, but they do not specifically explain workpiece burn [https://openalex.org/W3196394368||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9971052||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4322505914||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests nano-enhancers are considered better for workpiece burn mainly because they can enhance cooling, lubrication, and heat transfer, but the mechanism is not fully clarified and some summaries explicitly say the direct evidence is insufficient [https://openalex.org/W4206313494||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313508734||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) played the role of a solid lubricant nano-additive in canola oil, where it was used to improve the oil’s tribological performance because canola oil was described as having weaker tribological performance than petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The study tested hBN in canola oil at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% and evaluated the formulations by measuring dynamic viscosity, coefficient of friction (COF), and wear under boundary lubrication conditions using pin-on-disk tests [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. Among the hBN formulations, 1.0 wt.% produced the lowest COF, which was reported as 40% lower than base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also reported that combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelets in mixed nano-lubricant formulations produced a positive synergy, reducing friction by 56% and wear by 90% versus base oil, with the improvement attributed to a composite protective film and polishing mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, the other supplied papers are reviews that mention nanoparticle or nanomaterial additives in biolubricants or plant-based oils, but they do not provide canola-oil-specific hBN experimental details, so they mainly contextualize hBN as part of broader sustainable lubrication research rather than as a separate evaluated system [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4390658388||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4401870224||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports that hBN was investigated as an additive to enhance canola oil’s friction and wear behavior, with evaluation centered on tribological testing rather than broader application performance [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
final_answer: The clearest evidence comes from a Romania-specific study that uses the SDG Index to measure progress toward the SDGs at the local and regional level through an integrated subnational approach built on 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, the SDG Index is used to compare sustainable development performance across places within Romania rather than only at the national level [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. The results show strong spatial inequality: the highest sustainable development performance is concentrated in some specific geographical areas, while rural areas and extended peripheral regions in the eastern and southern parts of Romania are the poorest performers [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. This pattern suggests that progress toward the SDGs is uneven and that subnational monitoring can reveal territorial disparities that aggregate measures might hide [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers in the set reinforce the broader value of regional SDG monitoring, describing indicator sets as useful for benchmarking regions and guiding policymakers, while also emphasizing the need for robust data infrastructure and adaptive monitoring approaches [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001]. However, several other summaries do not provide Romania-specific or local/regional SDG Index results, and some are only about general SDG literature review, indicator selection, or non-Romanian regional trends, so they cannot confirm additional Romanian findings [https://openalex.org/W4284681716||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4389430761||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4312225363||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports that the SDG Index was applied as a subnational benchmarking tool in Romania and that it revealed marked east-south and rural-peripheral disadvantages in sustainable development performance [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
final_answer: The strongest evidence indicates that FTs do add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when acting as boundary spanners, and that this is not a purely mechanical compliance task [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. One paper explicitly distinguishes between compliance-oriented and improvement-oriented boundary-spanning actions, suggesting that FTs may either follow requirements narrowly or use them as a basis for proactive sustainability improvements [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. This role is also shaped by social capital, and focal firms are advised to build cognitive and relational capital with FTs before deploying SSD initiatives because the relationship between FTs and STs affects how sustainability is extended up the supply chain [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. Broader evidence from professional sustainability integration literature supports this interpretation by showing that professionals often understand sustainability as balancing environmental, economic, and social dimensions, and that perceptions differ across professional and geographical contexts [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000]. Related reporting and standard-setting studies also show that sustainability arenas remain contested and far from harmonized, with diverse actors holding different objectives and unwilling to give up their perspectives, which implies that boundary-spanning actors may interpret requirements through their own lenses [https://openalex.org/W4225388860||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4410729659||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, several papers do not directly address FTs or their personal interpretation, so evidence from boundary spanning, reporting, and standard-setting is only indirectly supportive rather than definitive for all contexts [https://openalex.org/W3157489939||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4289767614||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4313644972||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the literature suggests that FT interpretation is shaped by role context, social capital, and contested sustainability definitions, but the extent of interpretation likely varies between compliance-focused application and more improvement-oriented enactment [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the papers, organizational learning capability is portrayed as an enabler of deeper organizational change, but the direct link to radical innovation is only clearly demonstrated in one study. In that study, organizational learning capability fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, and it is described as an organizational context that promotes experimentation, dialogue, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and interaction with the external environment, all of which are linked to boosting radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper supports the broader idea that learning supports more transformative change by identifying learning principles tied to business transformation, including deutero learning mode, societal learning scope, and cooperative advantage objective, although it does not specify a direct radical-innovation mechanism [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000]. Related evidence shows that organizational learning is vital for sustainable performance and may work through intervening pathways such as organizational networking and organizational innovation, suggesting that learning contributes indirectly to innovation outcomes even when radical innovation is not explicitly tested [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||001]. Similarly, organizational readiness to learn directly influences sustainable economic performance and innovative work behavior directly influences sustainable economic performance, but this study does not address radical innovation and does not present organizational readiness to learn as a moderator [https://openalex.org/W3211385979||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from the ambidextrous-learning paper is consistent with the broader pattern that learning capabilities can support innovative decisions: top management team ambidextrous learning is positively associated with adopting sustainable business model innovations, and TMT diversity and university-industry collaboration increase ambidextrous learning [https://openalex.org/W4323928282||ABSTRACT||000]. However, other papers emphasize that the evidence base is indirect or incomplete, since some studies discuss absorptive capacity, organizational learning, or innovation capability without examining radical innovation specifically, and one paper suggests radical systemic innovations depend on proximity conditions rather than learning capability per se [https://openalex.org/W4320476375||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392624484||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the synthesis suggests that organizational learning capability contributes to radical innovation by creating a context for experimentation, external interaction, and deeper change, but most of the supporting evidence is indirect and concentrated in a small number of studies [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3119434529||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: Across the papers, the main public-health concern is that microplastics in fishmeal or fish feed can enter aquaculture systems and then move into edible fish, creating a pathway for human exposure through seafood consumption [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. One study in Bangladesh found microplastics in all commercial fish feed samples, with mean abundance of 500–2200 MPs/kg, showing that fish production systems can be exposed to widespread contamination through feed [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper explains that fishmeal made from by-catch fish is used in feeds for cultured fish and livestock, so contaminated fishmeal can introduce microplastics into ponds and cultured fish [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. These studies agree that the threat is largely indirect: microplastics may accumulate in cultured fish, alter fish physiology and behavior, and potentially reach consumers in edible portions [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. The broader reviews add that microplastics can persist for long periods, are difficult to fully understand, and may carry hazardous chemicals such as persistent organic pollutants on their surfaces, increasing concern about contaminant transfer through the food chain [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers also frame the issue as part of wider aquatic contamination and food-chain disruption, with downstream consequences for humans who consume seafood [https://openalex.org/W4295412833||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4311705688||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the evidence remains mostly inferential about direct human health outcomes from fishmeal specifically, and some summaries explicitly note that they do not provide direct fishmeal or human-health data [https://openalex.org/W4401805195||ABSTRACT||000; pmc_PMC9967563||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4408490507||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the literature suggests microplastics in fishmeal threaten global public health by contaminating aquaculture feed, disrupting aquatic food chains, and potentially exposing people to microplastics and associated contaminants through seafood, while direct causal health evidence is still limited [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001; https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: Across men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and chromosomal anomalies, elevated FSH is associated with a hypogonadal, testicular-failure phenotype that includes lower average testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher LH, greater height and arm span, and more gynecomastia than in the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. In a separate NOA cohort, elevated serum FSH and LH were observed in the failed sperm retrieval group, while the successful group had significantly larger testicular volume, and multivariate analysis identified serum FSH and bilateral testicular volumes as significant predictors of successful sperm extraction [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||001]. The KS group showed the clearest deviation from the undefined-cause group, with lower testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower testosterone, higher LH and FSH, and gynecomastia that was absent in the undefined group and present in more than half of KS cases [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Testicular XX DSD also differed from the undefined-cause group, but its LH, FSH, and penile length values were intermediate between KS and the undefined-cause group, and its testicular volume was similar to KS while other data were similar to the undefined group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. This pattern suggests that KS generally represents the most severe endocrine and clinical abnormality among the compared groups, whereas testicular XX DSD is partially shifted toward the KS phenotype but less extreme [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. One study also reported that certain Y-chromosome structural anomalies in men with NOA/severe oligozoospermia should prompt AZF deletion screening, including inv(Y)(p11.2q12), idic(Y)(q11.2), 46,XY,r(Y), idic(Y)(p11.2), and der(Y;Autosome) [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the provided summaries do not give stratified laboratory comparisons for all chromosomal subtypes, and one paper explicitly lacks evidence on KS, testicular XX DSD, or an undefined-cause comparison group, limiting synthesis across all anomalies [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The clearest evidence linking NEDD4 to the IGF1 pathway comes from the gastric cancer study, which separated GC cell lines into IGF1R-dependent and IGF1R-independent groups based on Akt phosphorylation after OSI906 treatment [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. In that context, NEDD4 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and NEDD4 overexpression promoted tumor growth specifically in IGF1R-dependent GC cells, indicating that NEDD4 acts in cells that rely on IGF1/IGF1R signaling [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study reports that a PTEN-IRS1 axis is required for this NEDD4-mediated regulation of Akt activation and tumor growth, and that NEDD4 promotes proliferation by antagonizing PTEN’s protein phosphatase activity toward IRS1 [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Clinically, NEDD4 was higher in IGF1-high GC tissues than in IGF1-low GC tissues and normal tissues, and co-high expression of NEDD4 and IGF1 predicted worse prognosis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate PDAC study also supports translational upregulation of NEDD4, stating that higher NEDD4 protein expression was due to an undefined mechanism involving translational activation, but it links this to PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling rather than directly to IGF1 [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the available evidence supports a model in which NEDD4 is upregulated at the protein level in some cancers and can enhance growth signaling in pathway-dependent cells, but only the gastric cancer study directly connects this biology to IGF1R dependence [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: Across the papers, textile waste management is consistently framed as a shift away from disposal and toward circular systems based on recovery, reuse, recycling, and reprocessing [https://openalex.org/W3205047951||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3206222416||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies describe waste conversion pathways that turn textile waste into valuable outputs, including recycled fiber production from post-consumer jeans and T-shirts, enzymatic fiber separation into purified fractions, and broader chemical or biotechnological conversion routes that support circular economy goals [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001]. The wastewater-focused review adds that textile effluent treatment is typically multi-stage and that adsorption is one of the most feasible methods for removing dyes and metals because of cost advantages and the variety of adsorbents available [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. This suggests a practical role for adsorption in managing textile waste streams, especially as a polishing or recovery step in wastewater treatment rather than as a property of solid textile waste materials themselves [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000]. However, most of the textile-waste conversion papers provided here do not actually discuss adsorption properties in textile materials, and several explicitly note that adsorption evidence is insufficient or absent [https://openalex.org/W3206222416||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4206622324||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also shows that conversion is constrained by material composition and contamination, since blends, dyes, and finishing chemicals can interfere with recycling and separation [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the strongest evidence supports using textile waste conversion to create recycled fibers, recover sugars or bio-oils, and enable cleaner processing, while adsorption is supported mainly for wastewater treatment applications linked to textile waste management [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4309710850||ABSTRACT||000].

final_answer: The district heating sustainability assessment paper compared five multi-criteria decision analysis methods: WSM, TOPSIS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE, and DEA, using eight criteria across 12 district heating companies [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Its sensitivity analysis varied criteria weights in three ways: individually across the stability range of alternatives, individually by a fixed value to examine effects on average scores, and by comparing AHP-derived weights with equal weights [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. The analysis and the literature review concluded that all five methods are suitable for sustainability analysis of district heating systems [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, the methods differ in their calculation processes and in how their results are interpreted, which means the choice of method affects the analytical perspective even if each is considered usable [https://openalex.org/W4220986058||ABSTRACT||000]. Broader district heating review evidence is consistent with the importance of MCDM approaches and shows that AHP is the most frequently used method in this field, but that source does not provide a comparable sensitivity test or method-by-method comparison [https://openalex.org/W4315708900||ABSTRACT||001]. Other supplied papers discuss MCDA or sustainability assessment generally, but they do not add district-heating-specific evidence on the exact method comparison or the sensitivity-analysis conclusions requested [https://openalex.org/W4281914972||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4311545548||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do the sustainability ideas in the supply chain management framework and the article on sustainable marketing both show how environmental sustainability can be advanced and linked to company image?
final_answer: The supply chain management papers consistently present environmental sustainability as something that can be advanced by moving beyond isolated actions to a broader systems or stakeholder view of supply chains. One framework emphasizes embedding a “sustainability mindset,” using a systems perspective to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals, and evaluating sustainability through “Knowing” and “Doing” while closing the gap in the missing “Being” dimension between what firms say and what they do [https://openalex.org/W4364359925||ABSTRACT||000]. Another study turns evidence from 86 studies into a structured framework of 789 sustainable practices within the triple bottom line, showing how supply chain practices can be organized into categories that guide industrial solutions [https://openalex.org/W4283697438||ABSTRACT||000]. A further paper finds that specific practices such as customer relationships, postponement, information sharing, and information quality significantly influence environmental sustainability, and that sustainability then improves financial performance [https://openalex.org/W3132273715||ABSTRACT||001]. Together, these studies suggest that environmental sustainability is advanced through internal management, supply chain coordination, and strategic orientation rather than through a single isolated tactic [https://openalex.org/W3128290205||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308101885||ABSTRACT||002]. They also show that sustainability is linked to company outcomes, especially firm performance and competitive advantage, which can support a stronger company image indirectly through better outcomes and strategic positioning [https://openalex.org/W3128290205||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4280505603||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the provided evidence does not include usable details from the sustainable marketing article itself, so a direct synthesis of how that article links environmental sustainability to company image cannot be made from these summaries alone [https://openalex.org/W4364359925||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308101885||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do sustainable technologies, such as clean energy in manufacturing and green and reverse logistics, support Industry 4.0 innovation and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises, and what did the analysis find about enterprise adoption and environmental management?
final_answer: Across the papers, sustainable technologies are consistently presented as enabling Industry 4.0 innovation by improving efficiency, reducing resource consumption, and strengthening environmental performance in manufacturing and supply chains [https://openalex.org/W4226256571||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001]. The clearest specific evidence comes from the study on clean energy in manufacturing and green/reverse logistics, which argues that these technologies create conditions for industrial development and future growth when combined with Industry 4.0 and SDG-oriented innovation [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. That same study also reports that, among 105 Slovak enterprises, more than 82% said they implemented the SDGs and more than 70% preferred environmental aspects in business management, with a significant relationship between environmental management under the SDGs and sustainability in production and logistics [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. It further found a statistically confirmed relationship between renewable energy technology use in industry and sustainability in logistics, reinforcing the link between sustainable technologies and SDG-based growth in industrial enterprises [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000]. More broadly, multiple reviews agree that Industry 4.0 supports sustainability and corporate growth, with reported benefits including better environmental performance, ecological support, and reduced environmental impact [https://openalex.org/W4398200114||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4389484631||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4311719782||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also frames this as a pathway toward Sustainability 4.0, where digitisation helps preserve energy and natural resources while contributing to a more socially inclusive and environmentally sustainable economy [https://openalex.org/W4282842216||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, the evidence is uneven: several papers offer only general Industry 4.0–sustainability claims without specific findings on clean energy, green/reverse logistics, adoption rates, or environmental management outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4392974914||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3170613256||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4389484631||ABSTRACT||000]. Adoption also appears context-dependent, since one study notes stronger sustainability adoption in developed economies with strong infrastructure and limited adoption in emerging economies [https://openalex.org/W3120619572||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the synthesis suggests that sustainable technologies and Industry 4.0 are mutually reinforcing, but the most concrete enterprise-level evidence is still concentrated in a single country case with limited detail on broader environmental management mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4280522772||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282842216||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does the study use predictive analytics in the 1-hop work, and what does the 2-hop AI impact assessment say about AI"s role for sustainable development?
final_answer: Across the 1-hop papers, predictive analytics is described as a practical AI capability used for forecasting and optimization: several studies mention advanced predictive models, AI-enabled predictive modeling, deep learning and supervised machine learning, and combinations of predictive analytics with machine learning and neural networks to improve monitoring, optimize systems, and support sustainability applications [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402735735||ABSTRACT||000]. These 1-hop uses are tied to resource monitoring, sustainable agriculture, waste and energy management, climate change applications, and cleaner production across industries [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4402735735||ABSTRACT||000]. In the 2-hop AI impact assessments, AI is generally framed as important for sustainable development because it can enable data-driven insights, optimizations, and solutions to environmental and SDG-related challenges [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4405499395||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the assessments are not uniformly celebratory: they emphasize that AI can both enable and inhibit sustainability, so its impact must be carefully assessed at the indicator level and through assessment questions or responsible governance frameworks [https://openalex.org/W3135629427||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4220935479||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers also stress that AI’s sustainability benefits depend on supportive policies, infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and responsible development, rather than on AI alone [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4392169541||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature further notes risks and constraints such as high initial costs, data privacy concerns, ecological footprint, bias, and the limited number of studies combining advanced AI with deep sustainability expertise [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4414098400||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the synthesis suggests that predictive analytics is one of the concrete mechanisms through which AI contributes to sustainability, while the 2-hop assessments portray AI’s role for sustainable development as promising but conditional, context-dependent, and in need of careful evaluation and governance [https://openalex.org/W4401831154||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4412514975||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3135629427||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How are the SDOs linked to policy coherance for sustainable development in the EU context?
final_answer: Across the papers, the SDGs are presented as a central framework for assessing and steering policy coherence for sustainable development in the EU, because they make it possible to track environmental, social, and economic dimensions together rather than separately [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000]. Several studies show that coherence is pursued by aligning EU strategies and instruments with the SDGs, including the European Green Deal, the Country-Specific Recommendations in the European Semester, circular economy policy, and Life Cycle Assessment as a monitoring and design tool [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W3209532954||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. The literature also suggests that the SDGs help identify where coherence is weakest: environmental SDGs are described as the most complex and least coherent, while interlinkages among EU policies, the SDGs, and planetary boundaries can be “existing, missing, or existing depending on the LCA framework” [https://openalex.org/W3134571733||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4210270578||ABSTRACT||000]. At the same time, coherence is not treated as purely technical, since one paper argues that policy coherence for sustainable development is shaped by political drivers such as ideas, institutions, and interests, and that technical arrangements may create an apolitical façade that limits transformative change [https://openalex.org/W4308113945||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4200315183||ABSTRACT||000]. Other papers reinforce this by recommending system perspectives, attention to trade-offs, and context-specific priorities across governance levels and scales of implementation [https://openalex.org/W4366975340||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the papers agree that the SDGs support policy coherence by providing a common reference point for alignment, monitoring, and comparison across EU policies and member states, but they also show that coherence remains incomplete and uneven, especially where political trade-offs, weak intra-cluster links, or missing policy coverage persist [https://openalex.org/W3194602120||ABSTRACT||001; https://openalex.org/W4366975340||ABSTRACT||001; https://openalex.org/W4312225363||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do the themes of "Environmental sustainability", "Sustainability implementation barriers", and "Sustainable residential buildings" connect when comparing off-site construction research with the barrier analysis in Ghana and the "Mostadam" approach in Saudi Arabia, and what sustainability-related findings are highlighted across these contexts?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, the three themes connect through a shared concern with how environmental sustainability is translated into building practice, especially for residential and affordable housing [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386401188||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001]. In the off-site construction evidence from Southern Africa, prefabricated construction methods were evaluated as sustainability-oriented housing solutions and showed higher overall sustainability performance, reinforcing the idea that modern construction methods can support environmental sustainability in residential buildings [https://openalex.org/W4386401188||ABSTRACT||000]. The South African housing-design paper similarly links sustainable design techniques, passive design, recycled and local materials, and socio-technical innovations to both sustainability and affordability, showing that environmental goals and cost concerns can move together in residential settings [https://openalex.org/W4385389240||ABSTRACT||001]. In Saudi Arabia, the Mostadam discussion frames sustainable residential buildings as a route toward broader sustainable cities and sustainable development, with practical strategies and future policies proposed for transformation in line with Vision 2030 [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001]. By contrast, the Ghana barrier studies show that implementation is constrained by different sets of obstacles: one study identifies cultural, economic, technical knowledge, and regulatory barriers to sustainable structural retrofitting, while another finds management, standards, society, and knowledge barriers in residential buildings, with management barriers the most significant [https://openalex.org/W4293340752||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||001]. The Ghana environmental-performance-indicator study adds that sustainability should be understood as a life-cycle issue and highlights water quality, air quality, energy use and conservation, and environmental compliance and management as especially important measures for building-project sustainability [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||001]. Taken together, the evidence suggests a consistent pattern: sustainable residential buildings are not only about design or rating systems, but also about the barriers, indicators, and implementation conditions that determine whether sustainability can actually be achieved [https://openalex.org/W3120903819||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4310036329||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3168941981||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the direct linkage between off-site construction research, the Ghana barrier analyses, and the Saudi Mostadam approach is only partial because several summaries explicitly note that they do not provide direct evidence for all three contexts together [https://openalex.org/W4386401188||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4293340752||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3145060410||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What did the interviews with retailers and service providers in North America reveal about managing product returns sustainably?
final_answer: Interviews with multichannel retailers, retail experts, and return service providers in the UK and North America found that retailers were mainly focused on the financial impact of returns and had little awareness of their environmental impact [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The interviews also showed that retailers generally lacked a comprehensive approach to reducing the environmental impact of returns, indicating that sustainable returns management was not yet integrated into routine practice [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The study further reports that the interviews helped identify barriers preventing retailers from developing environmental sustainability plans for returns management [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. Based on those findings, the authors developed a framework for environmental sustainability in returns management and a set of strategies to reduce the environmental impact of product returns [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. The evidence suggests that managing product returns sustainably requires moving beyond a cost-only mindset toward a broader sustainability framework [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001]. Related evidence from another paper notes that sustainability in reverse supply chains can be hindered by lack of governmental support and competitive pressures, which may help explain why such sustainability plans are difficult to implement [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the available evidence is limited to abstract-level summaries, so it does not provide detailed interview quotations, specific North American-only results, or a full accounting of all proposed strategies [https://openalex.org/W4317888257||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4322500966||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What hazard ratios were observed for incident diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidaemia after receiving Specific Health check-ups?
final_answer: The provided summaries do not contain observed hazard ratios for incident diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidaemia after receiving Specific Health check-ups, so those specific estimates cannot be extracted from the evidence. Several papers explicitly state that they do not report hazard ratios for these outcomes: one is a protocol that says SHC effectiveness has not been systemically evaluated and only plans future analyses of 10-year diabetes and hypertension incidence without reporting results [pmc_PMC10387623||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10387623||ABSTRACT||001]. Another paper discusses incidence of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and dyslipidemia being higher in one group but not statistically significant, while providing no hazard ratios [pmc_PMC9808887||ABSTRACT||001]. A separate study reports hazard ratios for mortality and cardiovascular outcomes by glucose category rather than for SHC-related incident diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidaemia [pmc_PMC9701417||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9701417||ABSTRACT||001]. Another summary likewise notes direct relationship coefficients for serum lipids, obesity, and blood pressure in women, but no hazard ratios for the requested outcomes [pmc_PMC9801602||ABSTRACT||001]. One study does report hazard ratios, but only for metabolic syndrome risk in hospital employees, not for the requested diseases: HR 1.936 in male middle-aged and senior employees, HR 1.969 in men with more than four family history risk factors, and HR 1.326 in women working shift duty [pmc_PMC10053111||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence base here is insufficient for answering the question as asked, because none of the summaries provide observed SHC-associated hazard ratios for incident diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidaemia [pmc_PMC10053111||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9808887||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC10387623||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9701417||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9801602||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What screening criteria and classification rules were used to select and categorize the 87 life cycle assessment studies?
final_answer: The clearest description of how 87 life cycle assessment studies were selected comes from the review that searched Scopus for 2017–2023 using the keywords “Sustainability assessment” OR “Life cycle assessment” AND “Internal combustion engine*” OR “ICE*,” followed by careful screening, and then retained 87 studies for analysis [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. That same review classified the 87 studies along six aspects: sustainability indicators, life cycle phases, life cycle inventories, ICE technologies including alternative fuels, types of mobile sources, and powertrain systems [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001]. Another systematic review used PRISMA with database searching and an evaluation matrix, but it did not specify exact inclusion or exclusion rules; its categorization was by life cycle approach, with 52 of 84 studies as stand-alone LCA, 8 as LCC combined with other analyses, and none as S-LCA [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate review of 144 articles on life cycle methods and quantitative methodologies restricted its search to peer-reviewed journal articles from 1960 to 2022 and used broad keyword groups covering life cycle methods and quantitative methods, but it did not explain how an 87-study subset would have been screened or classified [https://openalex.org/W4403910234||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4403910234||ABSTRACT||001]. The literature on circular life cycle sustainability assessment likewise relied on systematic selection criteria, but these were criteria for choosing circularity indicators—performance, loops, unit, dimension, and transversality—not criteria for selecting 87 studies [https://openalex.org/W4388662253||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4388662253||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests that the 87-study review used a keyword-based database search plus manual screening, then grouped studies by analytical dimensions of the supply chain and technology, while the exact inclusion/exclusion rules are not reported in the summaries available [https://openalex.org/W4393374431||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3130637975||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What thematic analysis procedure and inter-coder reliability metrics were used to analyze the interviews, focus groups, and observations?
final_answer: Across the provided summaries, only one paper clearly describes a thematic analysis procedure: it used thematic analysis on open-ended interview/survey responses to generate basic codes, then applied deductive coding to group sub-themes across questions into themes grounded in uncertainty management theory [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||001]. That study reported a detailed analytic yield of 727 codes organized into 92 sub-themes, 18 themes, and one meta-theme about uncertainty being stressful but manageable [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||002]. However, the evidence does not mention any inter-coder reliability metrics for that thematic analysis [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||001]. The other two non-reliability papers do not provide a thematic analysis procedure for interviews, focus groups, or observations; one used an iterative qualitative inquiry process with matrix-based case comparison, and the other was a systematic review focused on PRISM and RE-AIM abstraction rather than thematic coding [https://openalex.org/W3143930606||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4296954442||ABSTRACT||001]. Neither of those papers reports inter-coder reliability metrics in the available evidence [https://openalex.org/W3143930606||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4296954442||ABSTRACT||001]. In contrast, the remaining paper is about inter-rater reliability of AIS scores and uses intraclass correlation coefficients, but it is not a thematic analysis of qualitative interviews, focus groups, or observations [pmc_PMC10229665||ABSTRACT||000; pmc_PMC10229665||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence is insufficient to identify a common thematic analysis procedure or any reported inter-coder reliability metric for interviews, focus groups, and observations across the set of papers [pmc_PMC9890239||ABSTRACT||001; https://openalex.org/W3143930606||ABSTRACT||000; https://openalex.org/W4296954442||ABSTRACT||002].

query: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?

query: How are coronary artery calcifications associated with complications?
final_answer: Across the provided studies, coronary artery calcification is generally associated with worse cardiovascular prognosis and complications, but the strength and meaning of that association vary by context. In a review, CAC was linked to future ASCVD risk independent of conventional risk factors and improved risk prediction when added to a global risk model, although similar CAC levels could correspond to very different absolute risk across regions and ethnic groups [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000]. In symptomatic patients undergoing cardiac CT, higher coronary artery calcium scores were associated with mortality risk, supporting a prognostic relationship with death rather than specifying other complication types [pmc_PMC9806039||ABSTRACT||000]. In trauma patients, coronary artery calcification visible on routine CT was independently associated with in-hospital complications, and left main coronary artery calcification had an odds ratio of 3.9 for any complication [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. That trauma study also found that increasing numbers of calcified coronary arteries trended toward more complications and were significantly associated with adverse discharge condition, suggesting a burden-response pattern [pmc_PMC10229702||ABSTRACT||001]. At the same time, some evidence shows that calcification may mainly signal technical difficulty rather than direct procedural harm, because heavily calcified coronary lesions treated with orbital atherectomy had no primary safety events at 30 days despite lower device success [pmc_PMC10140256||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports CAC as a marker of higher risk for complications or mortality, but it does not prove that screening improves outcomes, and the complication risk is not uniform across populations [pmc_PMC5383538||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How does the combined detecion of KAI1 and VEGF improve the diagnosis of HCC?
final_answer: Combined detection of KAI1 and VEGF appears to improve HCC diagnosis by outperforming KAI1 alone on several diagnostic metrics in the reported study [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. In HCC patients, serum KAI1 was downregulated while VEGF was upregulated, and each marker showed disease relevance, with KAI1 linked to TNM staging and metastasis-related factors and VEGF linked to α-fetoprotein level [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. The ROC AUCs reported for single-marker diagnosis were 0.907 for KAI1 and 0.779 for VEGF, suggesting KAI1 had stronger standalone diagnostic performance in that dataset [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||000]. When the two markers were combined, sensitivity increased from 86.96% to 91.86% and accuracy increased from 83.06% to 84.68%, with negative predictive value reaching 78.79% [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. This supports the authors’ conclusion that the combined panel may greatly improve diagnostic efficiency and serve as a reliable biomarker set for HCC [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001]. However, the evidence provided here comes from a single abstract, so it does not establish whether the combined approach generalizes beyond that study or whether it improves other metrics such as specificity [pmc_PMC4164248||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did the learning curve for DIEP breast reconstruction change over time in this study?
final_answer: This study suggests that the DIEP breast reconstruction learning curve improved over time, but the pattern differed by perspective. At the institutional level, the main time-related change was a shorter hospital stay in the later cases for both single and double DIEP reconstructions, while otherwise there were no statistically significant differences between the beginning and end of the study period [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. In contrast, when the learning curve was examined for a single surgeon, there was a significant reduction in total surgery time over time, indicating greater efficiency with experience [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the findings imply that performance gains were more evident in operative efficiency for the surgeon than in broader institutional outcomes [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000]. The evidence provided does not include additional DIEP-specific studies showing a different time trend, and several other supplied papers explicitly do not address DIEP learning curves at all [pmc_PMC10364508||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364755||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10364779||ABSTRACT||000]. Therefore, the clearest reported change over time was shorter operative time for the surgeon and shorter length of stay for the institution, rather than a wide set of significantly changing outcomes [pmc_PMC10140818||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How do neonatal injury models help to know about adult hearts cardiac regeneration?
final_answer: Neonatal injury models are presented as especially useful because newborn mice retain a brief period of full cardiac regenerative capacity after injury, and this window may be relevant to the neonatal human heart [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. By studying this early-life regenerative state, the models help identify molecular factors that could later be used to stimulate endogenous cardiomyocyte proliferation in adult hearts [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000]. The same paper frames neonatal models as translational platforms for testing therapies, with findings from neonatal models, large-animal studies, and human insights together supporting regenerative medicine approaches [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. A related endothelial-cell injury study, while not specifically about neonatal models, supports the broader idea that examining injury responses and recovery can reveal mechanisms of cardiac repair and regeneration by showing that injury-induced endothelial changes can be transient and reversible [pmc_PMC9283358||ABSTRACT||000]. Together, these summaries suggest that neonatal injury models inform adult cardiac regeneration mainly by revealing developmental programs and repair mechanisms that are active early in life but diminished in adulthood [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9064850||ABSTRACT||001]. However, most of the other provided papers do not address neonatal injury models or adult cardiac regeneration, so the evidence base here is narrow and largely limited to one explicitly relevant summary [pmc_PMC10230358||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10149391||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9887753||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC8807455||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9889318||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
final_answer: The supplied evidence shows multiple, conflicting ClinicalTrials.gov records associated with studies named DECISION, so the exact record depends on which paper is being referenced. One DECISION phase III study is described as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in locally advanced/metastatic RAI-refractory DTC designed to test whether sorafenib improves progression-free survival (PFS) [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. In that study, treatment continued until radiographically documented progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent, with efficacy assessed every 56 days and safety every 28 days for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. Its primary endpoint was PFS, and secondary endpoints included overall survival, time to disease progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetic analysis [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001]. However, other summaries identify different DECISION records with different registration numbers, including NCT02709408, NCT03976804, and NCT05655715 [pmc_PMC5387979||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC9806070||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC9887717||ABSTRACT||001]. The most detailed later DECISION summary describes treatment followed by 10 cycles of nivolumab, with follow-up until progression, death, or 12 months after treatment, and co-primary endpoints of objective response rate and PSA response rate [pmc_PMC9887717||ABSTRACT||001]. That same summary lists secondary endpoints of safety, radiographic progression-free survival, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, PSA-progression-free survival beyond 12 weeks, quality of life, and overall survival, plus exploratory translational analyses [pmc_PMC9887717||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports that the record(s) labeled DECISION contain phase III designs with clearly specified schedules and endpoints, but the summaries do not resolve which registration identifier corresponds to the user’s intended DECISION study [pmc_PMC3164634||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9806070||ABSTRACT||002] [pmc_PMC9887717||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
final_answer: In the Iraq study, 1-day-old imported broiler chicks from Nineveh governorate were compared for maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination using 707 blood samples from 28 Ross 308 flocks and 17 Cobb 500 flocks [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The results showed that Cobb 500 chicks performed better than Ross 308 chicks, with 100% antibody positivity in Cobb 500 versus 97.78% in Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. Cobb 500 also had a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76) and a lower mean CV percentage (12.41% vs 15.18%), suggesting a more uniform antibody response [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||000]. The study concluded that both broiler types had high and uniform maternal antibody titers, but Cobb 500 produced chicks with higher protective titers than Ross 308 [pmc_PMC9805781||ABSTRACT||001]. The other provided papers did not address broiler chicks in Iraq or Newcastle disease maternal antibodies, so they do not change the comparison in this study [pmc_PMC10141882||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10330971||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9967544||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10059746||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How mask mandates help Covid-19 cases, and what did the study find?
final_answer: Across the included studies, mask mandates and mask use were associated with lower COVID-19 spread, especially when measures were sustained and followed by high compliance. In a US state-level analysis, mask mandates helped offset mobility-related increases in cases, and the authors estimated that a national mandate starting May 15, 2020 could have reduced total US infections by 23.7% to 30.4% by November 15, 2020 [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. That same study found mask mandates were more effective in states with higher compliance, suggesting that policy effectiveness depends on how well people actually wear masks [pmc_PMC9663388||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate duration-focused study found that keeping prevention measures in place for at least 2 months was associated with lower COVID-19 incidence than having no measure or one in place for less than 1 month, with mask mandates linked to larger reductions in more socially vulnerable counties [pmc_PMC9729715||ABSTRACT||001]. Mechanistically, another paper reported that masks can help prevent spread, and that combining a face mask with upward ventilation reduced indoor infectious concentration by nearly 99.95% compared with no precautionary strategies [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001]. Evidence from healthcare settings also supports masks as protective PPE: two reviews found that face masks significantly protected healthcare workers from infection, with surgical masks appearing better than cloth masks in one review and N95 masks highlighted as especially supportive of risk reduction in another [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC9190185||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9845060||ABSTRACT||001]. The studies also caution that masks are not a standalone solution, because improper use can be counterproductive and because vaccination, case identification, ventilation, and other preventive measures are needed to interrupt transmission chains [pmc_PMC9803700||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC9482873||ABSTRACT||001].

query: What role did hexagonal boron nitride play in the study of canola oil as a bio-lubricant, and what details are provided about its evaluation?
final_answer: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) was used in one study as a solid nano-additive blended into canola oil to improve its tribological performance as a bio-lubricant, with the authors noting that canola oil alone had poorer tribological performance than petroleum-based oils [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. The study evaluated hBN at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 wt.% in canola oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000]. Its performance was tested in a boundary lubrication regime using pin-on-disk experiments, where coefficient of friction and wear were measured [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. Among the tested concentrations, 1.0 wt.% hBN produced the lowest coefficient of friction and reduced friction by 40% relative to the base oil [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. The same paper also reported that combining hBN with graphene nanoplatelet in three nano-lubricant mixtures created positive synergy, reducing friction by 56% and wear by 90% versus base oil, which was attributed to a composite protective film and polishing mechanisms [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001]. In contrast, the other supplied papers are reviews or unrelated materials papers that do not provide canola-oil-specific data or hBN evaluation details, so they do not add direct evidence about this particular bio-lubricant study [https://openalex.org/W4327639096||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4306936325||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4386898801||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports hBN’s role as a friction- and wear-reducing nano-additive in canola oil, but only from a single study and within the limited test conditions reported [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4200600140||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
final_answer: In Romania, the SDG Index is used as an integrated metric to measure progress toward the SDGs at local and regional scales by combining a large set of indicators; one study calculated it from 90 indicators stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database, while another used it in a simulation model for Romanian cities to test cost-effective pathways to 2030 [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001]. At the local level, the city-level simulation suggested that the SDG Index can be used not only to score current performance but also to identify city-specific routes for improving all SDGs jointly by 2030 [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001]. At the regional level, related SDG-based monitoring work indicates that the framework can support benchmarking and help isolate environmental indicators to reveal areas needing improvement and to assess how policy frameworks contribute to environmental progress [https://openalex.org/W4390511697||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001]. The Romanian SDG Index results showed a highly uneven spatial pattern, with the strongest sustainable development performance concentrated in specific geographical areas [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. By contrast, rural areas and extended peripheral regions in eastern and southern Romania were the poorest performers, indicating that progress was not evenly distributed across the country [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000]. In the city-level modeling, the index suggested substantial room for improvement: 75.79% of cities could achieve 9–13 more SDGs by 2030, and the overall SDG index could increase from 74.57 to 97.49 under more intensive path adjustment [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001]. Other papers in the set support the broader idea that SDG indicators are useful for regional benchmarking and policy guidance, but they do not provide Romania-specific SDG Index results [https://openalex.org/W4399724167||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4206568419||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence suggests that the SDG Index is being used in Romania to identify spatial disparities, benchmark local and regional performance, and model improvement pathways, with the main finding being that development is concentrated in some areas while rural and peripheral eastern and southern regions lag behind [https://openalex.org/W3135800278||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4285599931||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How FT's do they add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements when they fulfill their boundary-spanning role?
final_answer: The evidence shows that whether FTs add their own personal interpretation to sustainability requirements depends on the specific setting and how the boundary-spanning role is framed. One paper explicitly states that FTs do add their own personal interpretation when fulfilling their boundary-spanning role, and distinguishes between compliance-oriented and improvement-oriented boundary-spanning actions [https://openalex.org/W3205987731||ABSTRACT||001]. Relatedly, a study of sustainability managers finds that boundary-spanning is enabled by individual values, multidisciplinary knowledge, and relational abilities, and that responses to conflicting sustainability and profitability goals are shaped by contextual forces and individual cognitive characteristics [https://openalex.org/W4390583545||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper similarly argues that professionals do not interpret sustainability requirements uniformly, but instead operationalise sustainability integration in ways that vary across professional and geographical contexts, leaving room for subjective understanding [https://openalex.org/W4313908265||ABSTRACT||000]. However, several other papers do not support a personal-reinterpretation reading and instead describe boundary-spanning or sustainability work in more general or structural terms, such as linking internal activities to environmental performance, responding to multi-level regulations and standards, or incorporating diverse perspectives through intentional practices [https://openalex.org/W3157489939||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4205454498||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4382811259||ABSTRACT||001]. Likewise, one paper on sustainability reporting notes that actors have diverse objectives and cannot give up their own perspectives, which suggests interpretation differences among boundary-spanners, while another says sustainability standards are shaped to serve state and industrial interests rather than being individually reinterpreted by FTs [https://openalex.org/W4225388860||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4313644972||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the literature implies that personal interpretation can matter in boundary-spanning sustainability work, but it is not consistently theorized or observed across all studies, and in many cases the focus is instead on institutional design, governance context, or intentional inclusion of diverse perspectives [https://openalex.org/W4304687713||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W3216416295||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How does organizational learning capability contribute to radical innovation?
final_answer: Across the papers, organizational learning capability is presented as an enabling context that helps translate leadership, sustainability, and CSR-related inputs into stronger innovation-related outcomes, though direct evidence for radical innovation is concentrated in only one study [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000]. The clearest radical-innovation finding is that organizational learning capability fully mediates the relationship between stewardship leader behavior and radical innovation, meaning it is the pathway through which leadership supports radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. That same study describes organizational learning capability as a context that promotes experimentation, dialog, participative decision-making, risk-taking, and external interaction, which are all presented as mechanisms that boost radical innovation [https://openalex.org/W3194620278||ABSTRACT||000]. Other studies reinforce the broader idea that learning capabilities improve downstream outcomes: organizational learning positively influences sustainable value creation and is strengthened by stakeholder engagement, while innovation capability also serves as an intermediate capability in that pathway [https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4400127182||ABSTRACT||001]. Similarly, organizational learning is described as important for sustainable organizational performance and as making innovation more informed and less disruptive when it is well-processed [https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W4378746192||ABSTRACT||001]. Additional papers support the broader pattern that learning-related capabilities help organizations adapt to new phenomena, such as sustainability, and improve performance, even when they do not address radical innovation directly [https://openalex.org/W4393229185||ABSTRACT||000][https://openalex.org/W3211385979||ABSTRACT||001]. query: How does global public health get threat from microplastics in fishmeal?
final_answer: The strongest direct evidence in these summaries is that microplastics can enter aquaculture through contaminated fishmeal or commercial fish feed, creating a pathway into fish raised for human consumption [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000]. In Bangladesh, commercial fish feeds were reported as fully contaminated with microplastics at mean levels of 500–2200 MPs/kg, which the study framed as a global public health concern because many developing countries rely on aquaculture fish for protein [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000]. Another paper similarly states that microplastics in fishmeal may interact with pond ecosystems, alter cultured fish physiology and behavior, and accumulate in edible portions of fish, potentially causing severe physiological disorders in consumers [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||001]. Several papers broaden this concern by noting that microplastics can persist, carry hazardous chemicals such as persistent organic pollutants, and act as a pathway for harmful contaminants through the food chain, with consequences for human health [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the evidence also shows uncertainty: one zebrafish study found no serious toxic effects from tested polyethylene microplastics because there was no internalization, although some biochemical markers changed [https://pmc_PMC9967563||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the summaries agree that the main public-health threat from microplastics in fishmeal is indirect exposure via contaminated farmed fish and potential food-chain contamination, but they do not provide direct human epidemiological evidence or a full mechanism for health outcomes [https://openalex.org/W4388496957||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4282929872||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408578227||ABSTRACT||000].

query: What clinical and laboratory findings are associated with elevated FSH in men with non-obstructive azoospermia and chromosomal anomalies, and how do KS and testicular XX DSD compare with the undefined cause group?
final_answer: In men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) and chromosomal anomalies, elevated FSH is linked to a more impaired testicular and clinical profile, including smaller testicular volume and severe sperm-production failure. One study found that in men with chromosomal anomalies, KS was associated with elevated FSH together with lower mean testicular volume, shorter penile length, lower total testosterone, higher LH, greater height and arm span, and more frequent gynecomastia [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. The same study reported that testicular XX DSD showed LH and FSH values intermediate between KS and the undefined-cause group, with penile length also intermediate, testicular volume similar to KS, and other data similar to the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001]. Another study similarly found that high FSH was common in KS and testicular XX DSD, with 90.9% of KS and 100% of testicular XX DSD cases showing high FSH versus 66.7% in the undefined-cause group [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. In that study, elevated-FSH cases with chromosomal abnormalities usually had small or mildly reduced testicular volume, and azoospermia or severe oligozoospermia was present in the evaluated patients [pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. Across these reports, KS appears more consistently associated with a broader hypogonadal phenotype, whereas testicular XX DSD is more variable and often intermediate between KS and undefined causes [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate NOA cohort also found that failed sperm retrieval was associated with elevated serum FSH and LH, while successful retrieval was associated with larger testicular volume and a higher testosterone/LH ratio, supporting FSH as part of a broader marker set for poor spermatogenic outcomes [pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||000][pmc_PMC10307674||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence suggests that elevated FSH in NOA with chromosomal anomalies tracks with reduced testicular volume and more severe reproductive endocrine abnormalities, and that KS tends to be more abnormal than the undefined-cause group, while testicular XX DSD is partly intermediate and partly similar to undefined-cause cases [pmc_PMC10065101||ABSTRACT||001][pmc_PMC10307663||ABSTRACT||000].

query: How is the translational regulation of NEDD4 linked to the IGF1 signaling pathway, and what does the context say about NEDD4 in cells that depend on this pathway?
final_answer: The clearest evidence linking NEDD4 to the IGF1 signaling pathway comes from gastric cancer cells, where NEDD4 promotes tumor growth and Akt activation in IGF1R-dependent cells through a PTEN-IRS1 axis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. In that study, NEDD4 knockdown suppressed growth and overexpression promoted it in IGF1R-dependent gastric cancer cells, while IGF1R-independent cells did not respond to either manipulation [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. This indicates that NEDD4’s effect is context-dependent and is tied to dependence on IGF1/IGF1R signaling rather than being universal across gastric cancer cells [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. The clinical context also supports this association, because NEDD4 is higher in IGF1-high gastric cancer tissues than in IGF1-low or normal tissues, and co-high NEDD4/IGF1 expression predicts worse prognosis [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001]. Other supplied papers do not provide evidence for an IGF1 link; one instead reports translational upregulation of NEDD4 in PDAC cells and connects it to PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling, not IGF1 [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||001] [pmc_PMC5386762||ABSTRACT||000]. Additional papers mention no NEDD4/IGF1 relationship and focus on unrelated pathways, such as TGFβ1/Smad4, eIF3i in angiogenesis, or Nedd4-2 in PDD-related glutamate transporter regulation [pmc_PMC5386959||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386737||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386455||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC5386455||ABSTRACT||001]. Overall, the evidence supports a specific role for NEDD4 in IGF1R-dependent cells, but only within the gastric cancer context provided here [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||000] [pmc_PMC10063445||ABSTRACT||001].

query: How textile waste management can use waste conversion and the adsorption properties in these materials?
final_answer: The papers consistently show that textile waste management can be improved by converting discarded textiles into higher-value products rather than sending them to landfill or incineration, which is presented as a core circular-economy strategy [https://openalex.org/W4205579211||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3169117693||ABSTRACT||000]. Across the studies, waste conversion routes include biological treatment with microorganisms and enzymes, chemical and biotechnological valorization, fractionation and separation of blended fibers, and molecular-level regeneration into new composite fibers [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308483537||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W3169117693||ABSTRACT||000]. Several papers also describe direct material upcycling, such as turning waste textiles into starch composites for sustainable furniture design or into secondary raw materials suitable for construction and geotechnical uses [https://openalex.org/W4321094467||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4205579211||ABSTRACT||000]. The more technical conversion studies report specific performance benefits, including up to 70% glucose recovery from acid hydrolysis, about 20% lower energy use with enzymatic recycling, and up to 25% higher bio-oil yields with fluidized-bed pyrolysis compared with fixed-bed reactors [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000]. However, the papers also agree that textile composition matters: mixed fibers, dyes, and finishing chemicals can hinder recycling or enzymatic breakdown, so pretreatment, repeated treatment, or tailored separation is often needed [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4323545673||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308483537||ABSTRACT||000]. On the specific question of adsorption properties, the provided summaries do not supply direct evidence that textile waste is being used for adsorption-based management, so that aspect cannot be substantiated from these papers alone [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4205579211||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4408599276||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4308483537||ABSTRACT||000]. Overall, the evidence supports waste conversion as the main management pathway, but adsorption-based uses remain unaddressed in the available summaries [https://openalex.org/W4407071446||ABSTRACT||001] [https://openalex.org/W4206677612||ABSTRACT||000].
